====================00c_1205_03.txt====================
*He comes to Inokashira Park after walking a short distance from the southern exit of Kichijoji Station.*
*The park at night is silent and still as death.*
*Reflections of the street lights quiver on the surface of the pond.*
*It's a beautiful sight.*
*It makes him want to sketch.*
*The nature of the inner city is different than the scenery he used to draw out in the country.*
*Even the _sakura_ tree that has shed its leaves seems somehow urban to him.*
*He walks over the carpet of snow to the _sakura_.*
*He lays his hand on the trunk.*
*The tree is perfectly still, but it's almost as though he can hear the pulsing of life from within it.*
*The _sakura_ that conserves its strength so its flowers can bloom in spring.*
*He wouldn't mind becoming nourishment for such a noble cause.*
*Was it Kajii Motojiro who said that there are corpses buried beneath the _sakura_?*
*He takes a small fruit knife out of a paper bag.*
*He made sure to choose one with a good, sharp blade.*
*It might have made the store clerk suspicious, but he doesn't care.*
*Whatever happens after this doesn't concern him, after all.*
*Light reflects off of the blade.*
*It's a pale, cold light, without a hint of warmth.*
*He observes his surroundings one last time.*
*No one is around.*
*There are houses and a shopping district just nearby, but the park is dead silent, not a soul in sight.*
*_...This is the perfect opportunity._*
*_I must do it now._*
*He pulls the knife across his wrist without hesitation.*
*He feels a throb, followed by a numb sensation.*
*It briefly looks like a mouth opening on white flesh.*
*Blood immediately pours out.*
*The pain hits him.*
*When he tenses his arm, a little more blood flows out, and he feels a dull pain.*
???: "...Oh, darn."
*He isn't bleeding heavily enough.*
*He tried to cut with all his strength, but he only struck a vein and some nerves.*
*He'll need to cut again.*
*Red blood falls on white snow.*
*_How filthy._*
*_It has to be more elegant, like flowers..._*
*He shakes his arm.*
*Blood flies everywhere.*
???: "Ahh, this is all wrong."
*He's let out a lot of blood, but it still doesn't resemble flowers.*
*He needs more blood.*
*He tries to place the knife against his wrist again... but slumps forward.*
*He falls face first into the snow.*
*He feels pain... but even more so, the cold.*
*_...I don't want to die in the snow._*
*Though it's too late for that thought now.*
*He can't help but think about his home town.*
*...A voice.*
*He hears a voice.*
*He turns his head in the direction it came from.*
*...There's a girl right next to him.*
*His vision blurs and the voice sounds like it's coming from far away.*
???: "...Why?"
*The girl's voice.*
???: "Why... are you trying to die...?"
*_...Why, you ask...?_*
*Before he has a chance to answer... his consciousness fades.*

====================01a_1205_00.txt====================
*...There was a girl named Kuchiki Toko.*
*I, Tokisaka Reiji, met her last year, in the spring of 1956.*
*I accepted a very strange request to help her "find her true self."*
*I thought it was a joke at the time.*
*But as I investigated, I found that the information she sought was quite complex.*
*During my investigation, she met with an accident.*
*She narrowly escaped death, but at a great cost.*
*A combination of a rare blood type and an incurable condition called aplastic anemia meant that she simply couldn't produce the volume of blood necessary to sustain her life.*
*Since her fractured limbs weren't likely to recover, they were amputated in a surgical procedure that allowed her to live with as little blood in her body as possible.*
*And before she even had time to stabilize... she was abducted.*
*It was a despicable crime targeting the assets she stood to inherit from a wealthy relative.*
*I was able to quickly solve that crime, but she never returned.*
*She was snatched away again by the serial murderer and novelist Katsuragi Shin.*
*He hid her away and neither I nor the police could find her no matter how frantically we searched.*
*We even caught the psychiatrist who may have instigated Katsuragi, Rokushiki Makoto, but interrogating him yielded nothing.*
*It's been almost two years since then, and I still search for her whenever I have spare time in between jobs.*
*But I've yet to find any clues... and my time came to a halt in the April of 1956.*

*I sit down on a bench near the pond.*
*Some sort of waterfowl is resting its wings on the pond.*
Reiji: "...Come to think of it, she used to come here to draw, huh?"
*I open up the sketchbook I brought with me from my office.*
*These are some of Toko's sketches.*
*The small shrine near the pond.*
*_Sakura_ in spring.*
*A bird flapping its wings.*
*A girl drawn with a nervous expression.*
Reiji: "Heh..."
*The nostalgia makes me smile.*
*The girl in this sketch is gone now, too.*
*An affable girl who used to be my sister's best friend...*
*I close the sketchbook and stand up.*
*The person I've been waiting for has appeared.*
Reiji: "...Hey, Chizuru-san."
*It's Kuchiki Chizuru, Toko's adoptive mother.*
Chizuru: "...Hello."
*I can tell just from her greeting that she's not exactly happy to see me, but I'm grateful that we could meet like this.*
Reiji: "Please, sit down."
Chizuru: "No... this is fine."
*She looks down at the bench and shakes her head upon seeing Toko's sketchbook.*
Reiji: "...I see."
Chizuru: "There are no new developments, correct?"
*Chizuru asks the question before I can open my mouth.*
Reiji: "...Correct."
*I nod.*
*Developments related to Toko's location.*
Reiji: "We have all of the police in Kanto looking for suspicious people. ...But we've found no new clues―"
Chizuru: "―Isn't this enough?"
Reiji: "Chizuru-san...?"
*Chizuru shakes her head slowly.*
Chizuru: "I know that she couldn't survive very long in that state. I can't burden you with this any longer, Tokisaka-san."
Reiji: "...I've never once thought of it as a burden. Besides... I'm not searching for her because you asked me to."
Chizuru: "...I suppose you're right. I can't just tell you to stop, can I?"
Reiji: "...That's correct."
Chizuru: "...Then could I ask you to stop making these reports?"
Reiji: "Is it a bother?"
Chizuru: "......"
*Chizuru doesn't answer.*
*Even if that's what she thinks, she probably can't say it.*
Chizuru: "...I'm such a selfish woman."
*Chizuru mumbles.*
Chizuru: "I can't help worrying more for my brother than her―than Toko."
*She, Kuchiki Chizuru, had certain relations with her brother in the past.*
*She loved her brother and tried to have his child... but in the end, her body was unable to bear children.*
*I hear it was related to the treatment of an illness.*
*When their father took pity on her, he had Chizuru adopt a child, and that was Toko.*
*I don't know how much their father knew about their relationship.*
*But I can't expose them to him.*
*...Because that's all in the past now.*
Reiji: "...I'll continue searching for Toko-san."
Chizuru: "...You're stubborn."
*Chizuru shakes her head and picks up the sketchbook she'd been averting her eyes from.*
*She's the one I'd received it from in the first place.*
Chizuru: "...I'm the one who encouraged her to really start drawing, you know."
Reiji: "Is that so?"
*It's the first I've heard of it.*
Chizuru: "I used to take pictures, myself. My brother gave me a camera as a present. This was before the war."
Reiji: "Before the war, huh?"
Chizuru: "Yes. I was sickly then, and went to the mountains, where the air was clearer, to recuperate. I took a lot of pictures there."
Reiji: "So that's why you encouraged her to start drawing?"
Chizuru: "...She seemed to really love drawing pictures. I think I just wanted to do something motherly."
*Chizuru lays the sketchbook back down.*
Chizuru: "...I'll be going, then."
Reiji: "Right... Be careful."

====================02a_0000.txt====================
*Slap,*
*slap,*
*slap.*
*Slap,*
*slap,*
*slap.*
*Small hand prints, like maple leaves, were left on the clay piled up on the offering stand.*
*The clay's surface was glossy, so it shined with the reflection of the candlelight.*
*Slap, slap, slap.*
*Rather than kneading the clay, she just hit it.*
*Over and over again.*
*Without uttering a sound.*
*There were six other identical stands around her.*
*All seven had the same lump of clay on top.*
*If one were to look closely, they would see little bits of something white buried in the clay.*
*And if they kept looking, they'd realize quite quickly that it was bone.*
*The soil had been collected from the seven graveyards in the vicinity of the village.*
*Such had been the custom for a long time.*
*Her hands stroked the surface of the clay, concealing the bones that emerged from the soil.*
*Slap, slap, slap.*
*After she'd finished kneading the clay, a new stand was prepared for her.*
*She scooped up the clay from the seventh stand into her small hands and placed it on the new stand.*
*She poured a little water onto it with a ladle and began kneading again with her palms.*
*Slap, slap, slap.*
*She mixed the soil together and continued kneading it until it became firm.*
*Slap, slap, slap.*
*The flames of the candles swayed.*
*Snow wasn't being blown inside, but the winter wind was cold nonetheless.*
*Her small fingertips were red and numb with cold, and she could barely feel the clay anymore.*
*But she continued kneading.*
*She knew the importance of this ritual.*
*Slap, slap, slap.*
*The moisture was absorbed into the clay and it became nice and firm.*
*She grasped the clay in both hands and shaped it into a ball.*
*As she rolled it in her hands, she molded it into the shape she had learned to make.*
*She gave it a neck and a head, and lengthened its arms and legs.*
*She formed grooves with her fingernails and made its face.*
*A crude clay doll that simultaneously resembled and didn't resemble a human being.*
*She was told that this was the shape of a human slumbering in its mother's womb.*
*She left it on top of the dirt that remained on the stand and took a piece of paper out of her kimono.*
*She picked up a knife and drew it from its sheath.*
*This was an important step toward completing the doll.*
*She placed the cold blade against her wrist.*
*The blade shook as it was pushed shallowly into her soft skin.*
*Though she was told it wouldn't hurt, it was still frightening to harm her own body.*
*She exhaled.*
*She shut her eyes, calmed herself, and gently pulled the blade.*
*She barely felt anything.*
*When she opened her eyelids, she saw a thin, red line on her wrist.*
*Small red orbs formed from the slit.*
*Red blood flowed from the cut.*
*She clenched her fist and turned her arm to the clay doll.*
*She dripped fresh blood over the mouth of the fetus she had just shaped.*
*The mouth drank in crimson droplets like a suckling baby.*
*Then the head, then the body.*
*The doll absorbed the blood all over, as if it were circulating throughout its body.*
*The crude fetus sucked up the blood and its body was stained black.*
*She wiped off the bloody blade with the paper in her mouth and restored it to its sheath.*
*She wrapped a cloth around her wrist to stop the bleeding.*
*There was a small paulownia wood box next to the offering stand.*
*The sides of the box were all about 21 cm long, and it was the perfect size for the clay doll.*
*She placed the fetus in the box carefully so as to retain its shape.*
*She closed the lid.*
*She stood.*
*Her body slumped forward and she stumbled a few steps.*
*But she managed to regain her footing and held the wooden box reverently in her hands.*
*She headed outside.*
*Slowly, she stepped onto the ground without putting her sandals on.*
*The night wind carried snow with it and chilled her to the bone.*
*She walked slowly on the path to the shrine, her breath white in the cold air.*
*The stone path had been swept clean, the snow pushed to both sides.*
*Still, the stones on the ground were as cold as ice.*
*She walked slowly so that she didn't slip.*
*She relied only on the light of the candles as she walked.*
*There was a section ahead marked off with _tamagushi_.*
*Only the center of that section had had the stone paving removed.*
*She bowed and kneeled on the pavement.*
*A hole had been dug where the pavement was removed.*
*The stands that still had soil left on them were lined up here.*
*She raised the box above her and bowed her head, placing the box in the hole.*
*After a prayer, she used both hands to scoop the dirt off of the stands and pour it into the hole where the box rested.*
*Tightly, so that there were no gaps.*
*She used the dirt from each stand to fill the hole.*
*Before long, the box was completely buried in the dirt.*
*Two adults came from either side of her and raised a flat stone above the hole.*
*The stone was fitted into the exact place it had been taken from.*
*She bowed her head low and stood.*
*This time, she didn't get dizzy.*
*She bowed twice, clapped twice, and bowed once in the proper procedure before turning back.*
*Slipping through the adults lined up before her, the Miko disappeared into the whirling snow.*
*Slipping through the adults lined up before her, the Miko―Satuki―disappeared into the whirling snow.*

*This story took place in what is now called the pre-war period...*
*In a mountain village where the snow piled up.*
*During the season when the cold winds blew from the Sea of Japan.*
*It felt cold enough to freeze, but at least the sky was free of clouds.*
*Of course, the clear sky made the temperature drop even lower, so there was really no winning.*
*Kuroya Naori walked home, these sorts of thoughts going through his head.*
*The settlement called Hitogata lay in the mountains on the border between the Toyama and Gifu prefectures.*
*The residents earned their livelihood through agriculture and sericulture.*

Takayama: "The Hinagami family is definitely special."
*Takayama stared at the Hinagami children, Ayato and Karen.*
*The Hinagami family had always ruled this area―Hitogata Village.*
*Even after the Meiji and Taisho eras, the Hinagami family still wielded influence behind the scenes in the area.*
*If they had just been village chiefs, they would have lost influence with time, but in recent years, they'd established a pharmaceutical company and brought wealth to the village.*
*Takayama could remember his father teaching him to show respect to the Hinagami family.*
Ayato: "Hey, isn't your mandarin awfully big, Karen?"
Karen: "I'm not sure about that, but... do you want to trade, Nii-sama?"
*...Of course, the successors to that family may not have been aware of that at all.*
Ayato: "Hey, Nao-chan, when are you gonna take us to this hideout of yours?"
Naori: "Don't bring that up here, stupid."
Takayama: "Hideout?"
*When Takayama asked, Naori made an uncomfortable expression.*
Naori: "It's just― umm... a thing in the mountains I made."
Takayama: "...Well, I get that you're at an age where you wanna do stuff like that."
*Takayama had once remodeled the shed at his family's house into his own space.*
*His father had found out and scolded him harshly for it, of course.*
Takayama: "But don't do anything dangerous there, okay?"
Naori: "Don't worry, I don't want to get yelled at by my dad."
*Naori's father Yuzuru had left the Hinagami family to marry into the Kuroya family.*
*So the Kuroya family also had some pull in the area.*
Takayama: "Well, I don't think you guys are up to anything bad."
Naori: "I'm honored that you think so."
*Naori smiled.*
Takayama: "We could go to war with the West at any minute, so if you don't stay in the village, you'll get conscripted right away."
*Takayama had meant it as a bit of a threat, but...*
Naori: "People with criminal records aren't conscripted, though. They would disgrace the empire, after all."
*...Naori had an easy comeback ready.*
Takayama: "...I― I know. I just don't want anyone disgracing the village―"
Naori: "Besides, I hear even though they do conscription physicals here, they don't actually recruit anyone."
Takayama: "Th-That's ridic―"
Ayato: "Is that true?"
*Takayama tried to prevent Naori from continuing, but Ayato butted in, pressing him for more.*
Naori: "...Well, that might not be true. It's just what I heard."
*Naori gave an ambiguous answer, perhaps sympathizing with Takayama.*
Takayama: "A-Anyway, you guys should just concentrate on your studies."
Naori: "I don't think I need to worry about anything in that area."
*Naori gazed at the rest of them.*
Takayama: "Are you gonna study medicine?"
Naori: "I've gotta take over the clinic, after all."
*Naori shrugged and picked up a mandarin.*
Naori: "We should head back now."
Takayama: "Ready to go study?"
Yu: "We should just do it here."
*Yu already had her textbook open by the stove.*
Naori: "I concentrate better in my own room."
Yu: "...I suppose you're right. Let's go, Ohina, Guriko."
*Yu interrupted the two of them while they were chatting away.*
Meguri: "Huh? Already?"
Yu: "You can talk about clothes whenever you want, can't you?"
Meguri: "Yeah, but― what, are you not interested, Young Mistress?"
Yu: "...Not really. What's the point of dressing up when you live in the middle of nowhere?"
Meguri: "We dress up because we've got no other ways to amuse ourselves."
*Karen nodded in agreement.*
Karen: "I'll tell you about what's popular in Tokyo next time. My father's going to buy me a magazine."
Yu: "...I'd rather read a literary magazine."
Takayama: "...So, weren't you guys going home?"
*Takayama urged the students, exasperated by their antics.*
Ayato: "We are. ...Come on, Karen."
Karen: "Yes, yes, I know."
*They all left the stove.*
Naori: "Well, see you later, Takayama-san."
Takayama: "At least bring business with you if you're going to visit."
Yu: "I don't think anyone would visit if they had to do that. It's peaceful here, after all."
Takayama: "Fine with me. It's better to be bored. Now get outta here."
*Takayama drove the students out and finally reclaimed his spot by the stove.*
*All of his mandarins were gone.*

====================02a_0200.txt====================
*A girl walked down a snow-laden road.*
*She stopped every once in a while and glanced at her surroundings.*
*She saw a building with a sign that read "Village Administration Branch Office" and a small police station.*
*She hesitated to enter either building at the moment.*
*It wasn't as if she'd done something.*
*But as a young girl, it frightened her to enter a place with a lot of adults.*
*Her fear was exacerbated by the fact that she'd barely ever held a conversation with a stranger.*
*All she'd wanted was to go outside for a bit.*
*She could see the building she'd left far in the distance.*
*She'd walked all the way from there on her own two feet.*
*She could hardly believe it.*
Satsuki: "...What should I do?"
*The girl―Satsuki―puffed out the words with white breath.*
*Her feet were numb with cold.*
*It wasn't bad enough to prevent her from walking, but her thin sandals were somewhat damp and her fingers felt hot, painful, and numb all at once.*
*If she huddled down, her clothes would get wet, so she couldn't do that, either.*
Satsuki: "Hahhh..."
*And just when she decided she should enter a building and ask to rest inside―*
???: "...Oh?"
*She heard a voice behind her.*
Satsuki: "Huh?!"
*She turned around.*
*There was a boy around the same age as her.*
Ayato: "Umm... Who might you be?"
Satsuki: "Uh, umm..."
*Satsuki lost her composure and her eyes wandered upwards.*
*She wasn't sure how to respond to that question.*
Satsuki: "U-Umm... I'm..."
???: "Are you a guest up at the Shigusa Shrine?"
*Another boy who looked to be a little older started speaking to her too.*
Ayato: "A guest?"
Naori: "Huh? You don't know, Rihito? I thought the Hinagamis would know more about this."
Ayato: "I haven't heard anything."
*The two boys conversed in front of Satsuki.*
Satsuki: "U-Umm... I want to get back to the shrine... but I don't know the way..."
*Satsuki professed timidly.*
Naori: "The Shigusa Shrine is just down this road and up the steps... but it might be hard in those clothes. I bet your feet are freezing."
Satsuki: "Y-Yes..."
Naori: "Carry her, Rihito."
Satsuki: "What?!"
*Satsuki yelped and looked at the boy who'd been called Rihito.*
Ayato: "Wh-Why do I have to..."
Naori: "It's the duty of a young Japanese gentleman like yourself to protect frail maidens, is it not?"
*His tone was teasing.*
Ayato: "I-I guess so, but..."
Satsuki: "U-Umm, I... I can walk."
*She couldn't be a bother to these boys.*
*Satsuki took a step in order to leave, when―*
Satsuki: "Aah?!"
*She tripped quite splendidly.*
Ayato: "Look out!"
*The snow on the road whirled up.*
Naori: "...You okay?"
*The older boy gave the two of them a dumbfounded look.*
Satsuki: "Y-Yes..."
*Satsuki nodded where she'd fallen.*
Naori: "Then could you stand? Rihito's gonna get squished."
Satsuki: "What― aah?!"
*The boy was sandwiched between Satsuki's backside and the ground.*
Satsuki: "U-Umm... I-I'm so sorry..."
Ayato: "...Nah, don't worry about it..."
*The boy stood and dusted the snow off his clothes.*
Naori: "This is his dream as a young Japanese gentleman."
*The older boy said, laughing.*
Ayato: "...No, it's not."
Satsuki: "U-Umm... Erm..."
Ayato: "...Here."
*The boy squatted and turned his back to Satsuki.*
Satsuki: "Huh...?"
Ayato: "...I might be a little wet, though."
*He urged her bluntly.*
*That was when Satsuki finally realized he was offering to carry her.*
Satsuki: "Ah, b-but..."
Naori: "Why don't you take advantage of his offer? Since he's going to the trouble and all."
Satsuki: "...Th-Thank you..."
*She placed her hands on the boy's shoulders and entrusted her weight to him.*
*He wasn't wet.*
Ayato: "Hm―ph."
*The boy stood easily.*
*He looked quite thin, but he was still plenty strong.*
Satsuki: "U-Umm... I'm really sorry, Rihito-san..."
Ayato: "It's Ayato."
Satsuki: "Huh?"
Ayato: "Hinagami Ayato. Rihito's my nickname. This is Nao-chan―Kuroya Naori."
Satsuki: "Oh, I'm... Satsuki."
Naori: "Hmm... Then is 'Sacchan' okay?"
Satsuki: "What?"
*Satsuki blinked.*
Ayato: "Nao-chan, should you really give someone you just met a nickname like that?"
*At Ayato's words, she realized that Naori had been addressing her.*
Naori: "It's more cozy this way. That's a good thing, right, Sacchan?"
Satsuki: "Um, y-yes..."
*Satsuki gave a hesitant nod.*
*It was the first time she'd been given a nickname like this.*
Ayato: "...Well, as long as you're okay with it. Let's go, then."
*Ayato started walking.*
*Satsuki hurriedly clung to him.*
*She could faintly feel his body heat.*
Ayato: "...Umm, that kind of hurts."
Satsuki: "...Oh, I-I'm so sorry..."
*Naori snickered behind them.*
*They walked along the path that had been cleared of snow and came to the center of the settlement, Kamihinna.*
Satsuki: "U-Umm... Rihito-san, I can... walk now."
*Satsuki said to Ayato when they came to a crossroads.*
Ayato: "You don't have to push yourself."
*Ayato said to her, breath white in the cold.*
Naori: "You should probably call it quits at the steps ahead."
*Naori looked up at the road before them.*
*The steps that led to the Shigusa Shrine went almost all the way up the mountain.*
Naori: "...Or do you want Sacchan to keep clinging to you?"
Ayato: "Stu― Of course not."
*Ayato crouched down.*
Satsuki: "Th-Thank you very much."
*Satsuki hurriedly climbed down to the snowy ground and straightened her skirt.*
Ayato: "Phew..."
*Ayato gave a big stretch.*
Naori: "Is this the first time you've been to the village, Sacchan?"
Satsuki: "...Yes."
Naori: "Then I'll give you a little explanation. First, this is Kamihinna, the center of the village."
*Naori spread out his arms.*
Naori: "The Kuroya Clinic where I live is right there, so come over if anything happens."
Ayato: "My house is in Kamihinna too, but it's a little farther away, toward Hidarihinna."
Satsuki: "Hidari...?"
*Satsuki turned to her left.*
Ayato: "No, that's Migihinna. We were just in Maehinna and the shrine's in Atohinna, so you have to think of it as if you're facing the entrance to the village."
*Ayato turned Satsuki around.*
Satsuki: "Oh..."
Ayato: "Now, my house is over here―on the left."
Satsuki: "I-I see..."
Naori: "People mostly live in Hidari, Migi, and Kamihinna. Maehinna has the inn, the village branch office, and the police station."
Ayato: "Well, shall we?"
*Ayato took the lead and started climbing the steps.*
*The steep steps had been carefully swept and were largely free of snow.*
*Still, it was a long way, so it was tough to climb up and down.*
Ayato: "The resident police officer, Takayama-san, always shovels these steps."
*Ayato explained from the front of the group.*
Naori: "He's got a crush on Saya-san, so he's pretty serious about his work."
Satsuki: "Really?"
*Satsuki asked, picturing Shigusa Saya, who had been taking care of her since she came to the village.*
Naori: "Well, if you asked him, he'd probably deny it."
*Naori laughed.*
Ayato: "That guy has a really weird serious side, so he'd probably say it was for the old man at the shrine."
*Ayato agreed.*
Naori: "That old man never comes down the steps, though. The old man at my house has to go to him on house calls."
Satsuki: "I see..."
*Satsuki didn't really understand, so all she could do was nod ambiguously.*
Ayato: "How long are you going to be here?"
*Ayato asked her.*
Satsuki: "Well... I'm sorry, but I don't really know."
*Satsuki shook her head.*
*She had no authority to decide how long she would be there.*
Naori: "I hope you're here for the festival in March. Right, Rihito?"
Ayato: "...Yeah."
Satsuki: "Festival...?"
Naori: "We have a festival on March 3rd to welcome the Miko. We start getting busy for it around New Years."
Ayato: "Do we?"
Naori: "...You really are clueless, aren't you, Rihito?"
*Naori muttered, exasperated.*
Ayato: "...Well, Grandpa and Grandma handle all that stuff. ...And here we are."
*Ayato finished climbing the steps.*
*Above him was the shrine's _torii_ gate.*
Satsuki: "Thank you very much."
*Satsuki bowed her head.*
Naori: "We haven't done anything since getting to the steps, though."
Ayato: "You didn't do anything before that either, Nao-chan."
*Ayato pouted.*
Satsuki: "Heheh..."
*Satsuki couldn't help smiling.*
Satsuki: "I get the feeling you two are very close."
Naori: "There aren't a lot of kids our age, after all. We've got a few other friends, too... I know―I'll introduce you to them next time."
Satsuki: "Oh...?"
Naori: "They're kind of noisy, but girls are supposed to get along with other girls, right?"
Satsuki: "I-I suppose so... I wonder if I'll be able to get along with them, though... I'm a little nervous. I've never really... had any friends before..."
Ayato: "I don't think you need to worry."
Naori: "Well, we can talk about that later. ...Looks like the welcoming party's here."
*Naori glanced toward the shrine.*
*A man and a woman came out from the shrine office next to the shrine.*
*It was the senior priest, Kensei, and his wife, Miya.*
Naori: "Hello, Kensei-san, Miya-san."
*Naori greeted them first and Ayato followed.*
Kensei: "Did you help Satsuki-san back?"
Ayato: "We did."
Satsuki: "I'm sorry for going out without permission..."
*Satsuki bowed her head deeply.*
Kensei: "I don't mind. I was thinking we'd need to introduce you to everyone pretty soon, anyway."
Miya: "Did you greet them?"
Satsuki: "Yes, both of them..."
Naori: "We heard Satsuki-san's a guest at the shrine."
Kensei: "That's right. We'll have her go formally greet the Hinagamis soon, so could you tell your grandfather, Ayato-kun?"
Ayato: "Of course."
*Ayato nodded.*
Miya: "Satsuki-san, Saya's waiting for you."
Satsuki: "...Okay."
*Satsuki nodded and turned to the two who had guided her here.*
Satsuki: "I'm terribly sorry for all the trouble I've caused you."
*She bowed her head deeply.*
Ayato: "Nah, I don't mind..."
Naori: "Let's hang out again soon."
*The two boys headed down the stone steps.*
Kensei: "Well then..."
*Kensei turned to Miya.*
Kensei: "We don't want you getting chilblains, so could you prepare her a footbath, Miya-san?"
Miya: "I've already prepared one. Come with me, Satsuki-san."
Satsuki: "...I'm terribly sorry."
*She sat down on the edge of the wooden floor and dipped her bare feet into a wash basin filled with hot water.*
Satsuki: "Phew..."
*She regained the sensation in her fingertips along with some pain and itching.*
Miya: "We'll have to rub them to get the blood flowing."
*Miya rubbed her feet with a towel.*
Satsuki: "...Thank you."
Miya: "You're our guest, so we can't have anything happening to you. ...Okay, make sure you dry off, too."
*Miya carefully wiped her feet off, making sure she didn't leave any moisture in between Satsuki's toes.*
???: "...What are you doing, Nee-sama?"
*Satsuki heard the voice from behind her.*
Miya: "I'm wiping off Satsuki-san's feet, Saya."
Saya: "There's no need for you to do something like that, Nee-sama."
*Saya walked briskly over to Miya and grabbed the cloth in her hand.*
Miya: "But... we can't have her getting chilblains."
Saya: "There's no need."
*Saya spat out the words and looked down at Satsuki.*
Saya: "Going out on your own like that... Even if Kensei-san gave his permission, that would normally never be allowed."
Satsuki: "...I-I'm sorry."
*Satsuki hung her head and apologized to Saya.*
Miya: "Saya..."
Saya: "I'm handling these things, so I would appreciate it if you didn't do unnecessary things like this, Nee-sama."
Miya: "R-Right..."
*Miya nodded and stood.*
Miya: "Satsuki-san, please make sure you dry your fingertips too, okay?"
Satsuki: "Oh... Y-Yes... Thank you."
*Miya took the wash basin and left.*
Saya: "...We're going back, Satsuki."
*Without waiting for her response, Saya grabbed Satsuki's arm and pulled her up.*
Satsuki: "Yes... Understood."
*Satsuki was brought to the room she'd been in since she came to the village.*
Saya: "...You are not to leave without permission."
*And with that, Saya left the room.*

Nanako: "Nnh... Phew."

*Though they were covered by a large coat, Nanako's breasts bounced when she stretched and Naori found his gaze glued to her for a moment.*
*He quickly averted his eyes.*
Nanako: "...Oh? What are you getting all red for?"
Naori: "Maybe it's your imagination?"
Nanako: "Oh, really?"
Naori: "It's just the sunset."
*The sun was long gone, of course.*
Nanako: "Guess you're right."
*Nanako smiled, nonetheless.*
*Naori wasn't sure whether or not she'd noticed.*
Nanako: "Well, Nao-chan, see you tomorrow."

Naori: "...I just can't deal with her."
*Night.*
*The Kuroya family had finished dinner and was relaxing in the living room.*
*Naori's father, Yuzuru, and his grandfather, So.*
*His mother and grandmother had both passed away, leaving the Kuroya family one of widowers.*
So: "...Ah, that's right, Naori."
Naori: "What?"

So: "Some time―early next year, I think―a relative's kids are gonna come stay with us here."
Naori: "A relative? Not a Hinagami, though?"
Yuzuru: "There'd be no point in us taking care of Hinagami relatives, would there?"
*Yuzuru, who had left the Hinagami family and took his wife's name, muttered.*
So: "It's two siblings from Chisato's―your mom's―younger sister's family. They want to recuperate in a place with lots of nature, so I hear."
Naori: "Lots of nature... That's pretty much all we've got here. There isn't even a hot spring."
Yuzuru: "It's not like a hot spring's necessary for recuperation."
Naori: "I know."
So: "One of 'em's a young lady, I hear. You'd better keep your paws off her."
Naori: "...Shouldn't we be saying that to you, Grandpa? You're the one always touching Nanako's butt."
So: "I'm just performing physical examinations!"
*So replied without even a hint of hesitation.*
Yuzuru: "...If we lose her, the clinic'll go under in a flash, so could you keep it under control, Dad?"
Naori: "...This is the only clinic around here, so I don't think we'd shut down without Nanako."
So: "Don't be such a fool, Naori. If Nanako-kun leaves, I'll drop dead in a flash."
Yuzuru: "...If you've got that kind of energy, I think you'll live 'til a hundred, Dad."
*Naori couldn't help but concur.*
So: "...Well, anyway, that's that. ...I hear it's starting to smell like war over in Tokyo nowadays, so they probably want to evacuate over here."
Yuzuru: "My brother said they haven't had any rice in the Toyko restaurants since summer."
So: "You just don't get that impression in the mountains of Toyama."
*Naori's father and grandfather carried on the conversation.*
So: "I've heard talk of a war starting with America, too."
Yuzuru: "Thanks to that, the bat's become a kite."
*Yuzuru grumbled as he toyed with a cigarette.*
Naori: "...Well, I've got studying to do."
So: "Sure."
*Naori returned to his room and opened up a book.*
*He wasn't actually studying, but rather, reading a novel he liked.*
*He planned on succeeding the family business and becoming a doctor, and his studies were going well.*
*But that wouldn't be for a long time still.*
*At the time, he wanted to immerse himself in the world of his daydreams.*
*He took out a sheaf of paper and ran his pencil over it.*
*He'd written a little, but not quite enough to call it a "novel" yet.*
*He was just writing down whatever came to mind, so he hadn't even committed it to proper draft paper yet.*
*When would he finish it? Not even Naori knew.*

====================02a_0400.txt====================
*The Hinagami residence, on the edge of Kamihinna.*
*Satsuki stood paralyzed in front of the house she was visiting for the first time.*
*It was much larger and more old-fashioned than she'd imagined.*
*She had of course heard of it before.*
*The Hinagami family controlled the settlement of Hitogata.*
*They were also called its founders since they had settled there with the Shigusa family in the warring states period.*
Kensei: "Is something wrong?"
*Kensei turned around in front of her.*
Satsuki: "No―I was just surprised, since it's much grander than I had imagined."
*She spoke honestly.*
Kensei: "The Hinagami family has brought the village prosperity for a long time now."
Satsuki: "I am aware."
Kensei: "Well―we can't keep them waiting. Let's go inside."
Satsuki: "Yes."
*Satsuki was led to a room and sat alone, waiting for the family head to come.*
*Kensei wasn't there.*
*He'd probably gone to arrange something.*
*The sliding door in the back opened and Satsuki straightened her posture.*
???: "...Sorry to have kept you waiting."
*A stately voice.*
*Satsuki didn't respond. She fell prostrate to the sound of the feet on the _tatami_.*
*And she waited.*
*Clothes rustled, and she could tell that he'd sat down on a cushion.*
???: "...Raise your head."
*Satsuki slowly sat up after being spoken to.*
*She saw an old man, deep wrinkles carved into his sullen face.*
Satsuki: "...I am staying at the Shigusa Shrine as a guest. My name is Satsuki."
*She bowed her head again.*
???: "I am the head of the Hinagami family, Hinagami Hideomi."
Satsuki: "I am aware."
Hideomi: "Hmph..."
*The old man―Hideomi―snorted.*
*Was that rude?*
*Was it a mistake to reply that way?*
*She was tremendously uneasy in front of this old man.*
*He was dignified... No, there was something more behind his intimidating air.*
Hideomi: "...Please enjoy your stay."
Satsuki: "Y― Yes, thank you."
Hideomi: "The festival is about three months from now... Until then."
Satsuki: "...Yes, of course."
*Hideomi stood.*
*She lowered her head again and waited, frozen, until he left.*
*The sliding door behind her closed, and Satsuki was finally able to breathe a long sigh.*
*That was all she'd had to do, but she still felt fatigue eating into her whole body.*
*She wished someone else could have taken her place, but that wasn't possible.*
*Going to greet the head of the Hinagami family was an important task Satsuki had to complete.*
*The sliding door opened again and Satsuki straightened her back once more.*
Kensei: "...Satsuki-san, it's me."
Satsuki: "Ah..."
*She saw Kensei and relaxed.*
Kensei: "You don't have to be so nervous. Hideomi-san is a kind man."
Satsuki: "But..."
*She looked up reproachfully at Kensei's smiling face.*
Kensei: "Hahaha... Can you stand?"
Satsuki: "Ah― yes."
*Satsuki took Kensei's hand, stood, and straightened her skirt.*
Kensei: "Well, let's head back. ...Or did you want to wait until Ayato-kun gets home?"
Satsuki: "...That won't be necessary."
*Satsuki shook her head.*
*She wouldn't know what to say to him, so she felt there was no need to see him again.*
Kensei: "Then, let's go."
Satsuki: "Yes."
*Satsuki followed Kensei out of the Hinagami mansion.*

*It was painful for Satsuki to sit silently at the place of honor in situations like this.*
*She could neither speak nor break her rigid posture. All she could do was sit.*
*Rioko brought a bottle of _sake_.*
Mariko: "Here you are."
*Mariko handed the two of them square _sake_ cups.*
Yoshimitsu: "...Humph."
Hideomi: "...Hmph."
*They both snorted as _sake_ was poured into their cups.*
*They started drinking the _sake_ without bringing their cups together.*
*Satsuki wished she could flee.*
Hideomi: "...Will the Miko be dancing for this year's festival?"
*Hideomi's gaze turned toward Satsuki.*
Yoshimitsu: "That's the plan."
Hideomi: "...How many years has it been?"
*Hideomi tipped his cup and drank.*
Yoshimitsu: "...It's the first time since the Showa era began."
Hideomi: "...It's been that long, has it?"
*Satsuki knew nothing about the past.*
Rioko: "...Here you are."
*Rioko poured _sake_ into his empty cup.*
Hideomi: "...We must prepare as well, then."
Yoshimitsu: "I'll leave that to you."
*The two drank cup after cup.*
*Having no idea what was going on, all Satsuki could do was remain stiffly silent.*

Ayato: "Hmm... It's not that I want to draw something religious, I'm just looking for some new material."
Naori: "How about something like folklore, then? There's plenty of that around here, right?"
Ayato: "But that kinda stuff is..."
*Ayato was evasive.*
Naori: "I bet you'll be able to find plenty just by asking your family."
Ayato: "...And that's why I'd rather not. I mean... it always ends up being about our ancestors or whatever."
Naori: "The ancestors of the Hinagami family... Weren't they vassals of the Maeda family?"
Ayato: "More like vassals of vassals, I think. They were from a sub-fief."
Naori: "And any anecdotes from around then... would be about 'Hinna-sama,' right?"
Ayato: "I don't know anything for sure, though. I doubt they'll formally tell me anything until I succeed the family."
Naori: "Come to think of it, my dad doesn't really know that much about the Hinagami family or Hinna-sama, either."
*Naori's father Yuzuru was the second son, and didn't possess the qualifications to succeed the family.*
Ayato: "By the way, Nao-chan..."
*He turned to face Naori.*
Naori: "What is it?"
Ayato: "The festival's coming up, right? Grandpa said that the Miko would be in it this year..."
Naori: "Yeah... I heard that too."
Ayato: "I... don't suppose this Miko might be Sacchan?"
Naori: "I don't know, either. Sacchan's a visiting 'guest,' right? But the Miko is supposed to be in Hitogata purifying herself forever."
Ayato: "Yeah, but..."
*Ayato seemed indecisive, as if he was thinking about something.*
Naori: "...Well, if you're that worried about it, why don't you just go ask her? She's right over there."
Ayato: "Huh?!"
*In the direction Naori had pointed―at the base of the stone steps leading to the Shigusa Shrine―Satsuki stood, wearing a beautiful kimono.*
Ayato: "Ah..."
Satsuki: "Hello."
*Satsuki bowed.*
Naori: "Hey. It looks like Rihito has a question for you."
*Naori said, gesturing at Ayato.*
Satsuki: "Oh? What is it?"
*Seemingly surprised, Satsuki tilted her head.*
Ayato: "N-No, it's not that important, and I―"
*Ayato retreated.*
Naori: "There's no need to be nervous. It's just a little gossip."
*Naori gave Ayato a shove, pushing him in front of Satsuki.*
Satsuki: "What is it...?"
Ayato: "Oh, umm... There's a rumor going around that you're the Miko. ...Though Nao-chan was the one who started it."
Naori: "No I didn't."
*Naori poked Ayato's head from behind him.*
Satsuki: "I'm... the Miko...?"
Ayato: "Oh, but it was just a rumor. I mean, I hear no one has ever seen what the Miko looks like up until now..."
Naori: "That's because she appears during the festival wearing a mask. I hear Saya-san has been doing it as a stand-in since we were little, though."
Satsuki: "I see..."
*Satsuki didn't seem to understand.*
*If she had really come from outside the village, then that was no wonder.*
Satsuki: "Umm... what exactly happens at the festival?"
Naori: "Well, let's see... The main reason for the festival would be the _Kagura_ dance, right?"
*He confirmed with Ayato.*
*He figured someone from the Hinagami family would know more about this sort of thing.*
Ayato: "There isn't much, but they put up some stands on the shrine grounds. You can get candied apples and _ohagi_, stuff like that."
Naori: "...That's not the reason for the festival, that's your reason."
Satsuki: "Heheh... Sounds fun."
*Satsuki smiled.*
Naori: "Well, it's pretty much the only event in the whole settlement. We don't really have much to amuse ourselves with here."
Ayato: "You'll come to see it, right, Sacchan?"
Satsuki: "...Huh? Me?"
Ayato: "The festival's on March 3rd. You'll still be here by then, right?"
Satsuki: "Yes... Most likely. I've never been to a festival before, so I'm looking forward to it..."
Ayato: "It'd be nice if we could go together, don't you think?"
Satsuki: "...Yes, I suppose so."
*Satsuki nodded, blushing.*

====================02a_1110.txt====================
*By the time Satsuki got back to the shrine, snow had started falling from the sky.*
*Apparently they would put stands here during the festival.*
*Satsuki didn't know if she'd be able to see them, so all she could do was imagine them.*
Satsuki: "...But I've never been to a festival before."
*She said to herself.*
*Festivals had had nothing to do with any place Satsuki had been up until now.*
*She had never been allowed anywhere that lively.*
Satsuki: "But even if I've never been to one, I can still imagine, right?"
*She responded to her own words.*
*It was as if she was having a conversation.*
Satsuki: "...I don't know. What are 'stands'? Some kind of shop...? He did say they had _ohagi_..."
*She recalled what Rihito had said earlier.*
*He'd invited Satsuki to the festival.*
*She was happy for the invitation.*
*However...*
Satsuki: "...Will I be able to go...?"
*Satsuki couldn't answer that question.*
Saya: "Satsuki-san."
*Instead, Saya's voice stopped her.*
Satsuki: "I have returned."
*She bowed her head to Saya.*
Saya: "Welcome back. Nothing happened?"
Satsuki: "Yes."
*A curt response.*
*She didn't mention that she had met Rihito and Nao-chan.*
Saya: "You have dancing practice today, so come by my room later."
Satsuki: "Yes, understood."
*Satsuki bowed and headed for the shrine office.*
*She passed by it and headed to the backyard.*
*This was the separated storehouse given to Satsuki.*
*She unlocked the door and entered.*
*It was midday, and yet inside the storehouse, it was dark.*
*"...I'm back."*
*She said, closing the door.*
*Dinner had already been laid out on the _tatami_.*
*Before taking her seat, Satsuki headed to the large mirror in the back of the room.*
*"I'm back."*
*She repeated herself in front of the mirror.*
*"Welcome back."*
*Satsuki's mouth moved.*
*"How was your day?"*
*She was asked a question.*
*"I heard about the festival."*
*"Festival?"*
*"Yes, Rihito-san told me about it."*
*"...I see."*
*The Satsuki reflected in the mirror nodded.*
*"Have some supper. It'll get cold."*
*"Yes, I suppose you're right."*
*She left the mirror and sat on a woven cushion.*
*The meal consisted of boiled barley, sardines, and miso soup with potato, meat, and radish.*
*Some rice was mixed in with the barley.*
*"...My gratitude."*
*She entwined her fingers and offered a short prayer.*
*It was a habit that had been engrained in her since childhood.*
*She picked up her chopsticks and began to eat.*
*It may have been a little while since the serving table was brought to her, as the food was already mostly cold.*
*Still, she was thankful for the food as she brought it to her stomach.*
*"...It was delicious."*
*After finishing the miso soup, she offered another prayer.*
*"Well, I have my dancing practice."*
*She said, gathering up her dishes and the serving table.*
*"Yes, I know."*
*Satsuki left the storehouse.*
*The backyard was covered in snow, and the path to the shrine office was faintly illuminated.*
*She hurried to the office, table in her arms.*
*Satsuki put the table in the kitchen before heading to Saya's room as she'd been told to.*
Saya: "Welcome, Satsuki-san."
*She took a seat in front of Saya.*
Satsuki: "...Sorry for the wait."
Saya: "Let's begin."
*Saya stood.*
Saya: "Do you remember the footwork?"
Satsuki: "Y-Yes... For the most part."
Saya: "We've still got some time, so don't rush. Take your time remembering everything."
*Saya smiled and slowly began the basic footwork of the dance.*
Saya: "Forward... Back..."
*Saya's feet moved with her voice.*
Saya: "Turn... Crouch..."
*Saya's movements were graceful.*
*Satsuki stiffly watched her footwork.*
*She couldn't move like that yet, so she made sure to burn Saya's movements into her mind.*
Saya: "...Okay, Satsuki-san."
Satsuki: "Right..."
*Satsuki stood.*
Saya: "Forward... Back..."
*Satsuki moved with Saya's voice.*
Saya: "Turn―yes, and crouch..."
*She faithfully mimicked Saya's earlier movements.*
Saya: "Keep your torso like that―yes, now move to the side, and turn..."
*She turned on one leg.*
Saya: "Feet straight, fingers like you're drawing a circle..."
*Saya instructed her at points.*
Saya: "Hands forward... Elbows straight, don't bend them..."
*Saya rose and stood behind Satsuki.*
Saya: "Now raise your arm―yes, like that."
*Saya took Satsuki's arm and raised it above her head.*
Saya: "Fingers out straight."
*Satsuki's hand rested in Saya's.*
Saya: "Yes―waist straight..."
*Saya spoke into Satsuki's ear.*
Saya: "Now, slowly, down..."
*Saya's body leaned over Satsuki's.*
Saya: "...And that's it."
Satsuki: "R― Right..."
*Saya pulled Satsuki's body back up.*
Saya: "Once more, from the beginning."
Satsuki: "...Understood."
*Saya left Satsuki's side and took a seat in the corner of the room.*
Saya: "Begin. Forward... Back..."
*Satsuki moved with Saya's voice.*
*The light of the candle flickered, and Satsuki's shadow was cast upon the sliding door.*
*Satsuki continued practicing her dance, showing her shadow as if it were her other self.*

====================02b_0100.txt====================
*It was February.*
*The festival at the beginning of March was coming up and the inhabitants of the village were focused on its preparation.*
*_Shimenawa_ and _tamagushi_ were displayed in every house and sacred _sake_ was being brought in to be offered.*
*Nanako watched it all with a bit of disillusionment in her eyes.*
*The village elderly had always gone about preparing for the festival without a moment of hesitation.*
*Even at the hospital, they talked excitedly about how this would be the first time in many years that the Miko would attend the festival.*
*Nanako wondered what it all meant.*
*If it was going to cause a miracle, maybe it would free this country from the circumstances bearing down around it.*
*The war on the mainland was causing shortages of goods within the country and would eventually result in the deprivation of the people's freedom.*
*...But she knew that a regional god didn't possess that sort of power.*
*It might have even been too much to ask for a miracle that the people of this village weren't conscripted as soldiers.*
Nanako: "...I'm back."
*She set the bread she'd bought at the settlement's only general store on the table.*
*She found So, Naori, and their guest, Fumiya, in the living room.*
So: "Sorry to trouble you all the time, Nanako-kun."
Nanako: "I thought we agreed not to say that."
*Evading So's hand as it reached toward her butt, Nanako sat in a chair.*
Nanako: "Everyone's busy preparing for the festival, huh?"
So: "Well, it's been so long since the Miko's offered a dance."
*So said as he tore off some bread from a bun.*
Naori: "When was the last time the Miko was there?"
So: "...About 20 years ago."
*So answered, staring up at the ceiling.*
Fumiya: "What sort of things go on at the festival?"
So: "...The dance, mostly. Otherwise, there are some food stands, I suppose."
Naori: "Do we really need to have it in winter, though?"
So: "Well, it's supposed to be on the same day as Hinamatsuri."
Fumiya: "How are the two related?"
So: "Because of Hinna-sama."
*So explained to Fumiya.*
Naori: "But Hinna-sama is the guardian deity of the Hinagamis, right?"
So: "Mm. Back then, everyone thought the prosperity of the chief of the village, Hinagami, was directly related to the growth of the village itself. And that's still true now, isn't it?"
Nanako: "...I suppose so."
*Nanako agreed.*
*If Hinagami Pharmaceuticals wasn't earning money on the outside, the tiny settlement would probably disappear in the blink of an eye.*
*The extent of their contributions were immeasurable precisely because of the remoteness of the area.*
Fumiya: "So, in what ways does the 'Miko' differ from a regular shrine maiden?"
So: "Not many. The Miko is an agent of Hinna-sama. Shrine maidens in other places do things like channeling, right? Something along those lines."
Fumiya: "I see..."
So: "I may be learned in the art of medicine, but I don't know much about Shinto. I'm just repeating what I've heard since long ago."
*So said with a laugh.*
Naori: "They say there's a curse, too."
Fumiya: "A... curse?"
So: "Mm... Well, so they say."
*So kept his words brief.*
So: "It's nothing to worry about if you just live your life normally."
Naori: "Do you have to do something to be cursed?"
*Naori continued to pry with his questions.*
So: "If you worship Hinna-sama properly, you'll be blessed, but if you worship incorrectly, disaster will befall you, or so it goes."
*Yuzuru emerged from the examination room.*
Yuzuru: "Someone took the 'disaster' part and exaggerated it into a curse―that's what happened."
*Chizuru was at Yuzuru's side.*
Nanako: "Chizuru-san... is something wrong?"
*She looked sickly.*
Chizuru: "I just... don't feel very well..."
Yuzuru: "I gave her a soporific, so she should rest for a while in her room."
Nanako: "Got it."
Fumiya: "Oh, I'll take her."
*Fumiya stood.*
Nanako: "Okay, I appreciate it."
*He supported Chiruzu's body and the two of them left the living room, huddled together.*
Yuzuru: "―Chizuru-san might need some psychiatric treatment, too."
*Yuzuru muttered.*
So: "Is it bad?"
Yuzuru: "She's still showing signs of insomnia. I believe it's placing a physical burden on her as well."
So: "Well, I'll leave that to you, Yuzuru."
Yuzuru: "Right―and could you watch out for her too, Sawashiro-kun?"
Nanako: "Yes, I understand."
*Nanako nodded, though she got the feeling that Chizuru wasn't very comfortable around her.*

====================02b_0110.txt====================
*Satsuki walked the road that led to the shrine.*
*She made sure there was no one in front of nor behind her and stepped past a _shimenawa_ onto a side road.*
*The area behind the rope was sacred ground, off limits to entry.*
*She walked down the narrow path through the grove.*
*After walking for a time, a cave appeared before her.*
*A _shimenawa_ hung here, too.*
*This area was called Kakurebina, and was the deepest part of the settlement.*
*She'd gone a short ways up the mountain, but this wasn't her destination.*
*A stream flowed just nearby.*
*It wasn't deep, but it continued flowing without freezing, even in winter.*
*She followed the water downstream.*
*The snow around the bank had melted, exposing the stones and making the path a lot easier to walk than it had seemed.*
*But she proceeded slowly, so as to not slip into the water.*
*This was a secret path she'd found that only she knew about.*
*She looked up at the sky as she walked.*
*With the trees bare of leaves, she could see relatively far through the grove.*
*Farther downstream she could see a familiar building.*
Satsuki: "...Phew."
*When she arrived in front of the hideout, she breathed a sigh.*
*Her calves were a little sore from the walk.*
*She'd had the idea to look for this path after being brought to the hideout before, but taking the stone steps like usual may have been quicker.*
*...And her feet hurt.*
*When she put her hand on the door to enter the hideout, she noticed Ayato in the opposite direction from the way she'd come.*
Satsuki: "Oh..."
*He was here.*
*When she saw him, she was so happy she almost ran to him... but she stopped.*
*His profile.*
*He was staring at a single point with a thoughtful expression.*
*A small sketchbook was in his hands.*
*He was drawing.*
*She wondered what he was drawing and followed his line of sight, but all Satsuki saw was a field of snow.*
*Or rather―just then, the snow moved slightly.*
*Small black eyes darted about.*
*It was a snow-white bird.*
*It poked at tree roots and the snow with a small beak.*
*Satsuki didn't dare move.*
*She imagined that if she moved even a little, the white bird would notice her.*
*She wanted to ask Ayato what kind of bird it was, but she couldn't even speak.*
*She peered out from behind the wall, watching Ayato and the bird.*
*It looked like Ayato was drawing the bird.*
*Pencil in hand, his body didn't even twitch, save for his eyes and fingers.*
*Satsuki held her breath as well, stiffly watching Ayato and the white bird.*
*The white bird lifted its head.*
Ayato: "Ah..."
*At almost exactly the same moment Ayato gasped, the bird spread its wings and took flight.*
*It moved its small wings and kicked off of the ground to fly away.*
Ayato: "...Haah."
*Ayato sighed.*
Satsuki: "Rihito-san."
*Satsuki could finally speak to him.*
Ayato: "Oh, Sacchan."
*Finally noticing her, Ayato walked over.*
Satsuki: "What kind of bird was that?"
*She asked the question she'd been wanting to ask.*
Ayato: "Oh, it was a ptarmigan. They're usually on taller mountains, but this one came down here―I was sketching it, since it's a rare sight."
Satsuki: "I see... It was a beautiful bird."
Ayato: "They're only white in winter, though. In summer, they're darker."
Satsuki: "Really... Umm, would you mind showing me your sketch?"
Ayato: "It's not finished, but... sure."
*Ayato handed over his sketchbook.*
Satsuki: "Thank you."
*She thought Ayato's ptarmigan sketch captured the features of the bird very well.*
*A round body and small, round eyes.*
Satsuki: "Wow... It's beautiful."
Ayato: "You think so...?"
*Ayato scratched his nose and looked away as if embarrassed.*
Satsuki: "Yes. I mean, for you to draw all this... in such a short time..."
Ayato: "...Well, I've always liked drawing."
Satsuki: "Umm, can I... have this...?"
Ayato: "Nope."
Satsuki: "Huh...?"
Ayato: "...It's not done yet. I can't give you something incomplete."
Satsuki: "I-I see..."
*Satsuki hung her head.*
Ayato: "But if I see another ptarmigan and finish it, it's all yours."
*Ayato murmured.*
Satsuki: "Really?"
Ayato: "...There's no point in lying about it, is there?"
Satsuki: "Then it's a promise, right?"
*She beamed.*
*For Satsuki, who had so few possessions, she knew it would be an irreplaceable treasure.*
Satsuki: "Then we'll have to find another ptarmigan right away."
Ayato: "...It's a rare sight here as it is, so it won't be that easy."
*A little discouraged by his words, Satsuki gazed out over the snow fields.*

====================02b_0300.txt====================
*Chizuru sat in her room, dazed.*
*Next to her lay her brother Fumiya, wrapped in a blanket.*
*His injury was more severe than she had thought―the damage to the tendons and blood vessels was so extensive that the tips of the middle, ring, and little fingers on his right hand had had to be amputated.*
*Her brother had been planning to follow in their father's footsteps and become a surgeon.*
*The damage to the fingers on his dominant hand meant he'd no longer be able to hold a scalpel.*
*Of course, So, who'd performed the operation, had said that it may still be possible with training.*
*But the shock had been too much for Fumiya―who was just about to go into his field of study―and he'd been confining himself to his bed ever since the accident.*
*At the time, when So and Nanako had asked her what had happened, all Chizuru could say was:*
*_It's my fault._*
*She couldn't say any more than that.*
Chizuru: "...Nii-san."
*She softly laid a hand on the blanket covering her brother.*
*He twitched, but that was the extent of his movement.*
Chizuru: "......"
*A sigh escaped her lips.*
*Chizuru didn't know what to do.*
*All she could do was be by his side like this.*
*But... when she thought about what had happened... she wondered if the act of being by his side itself was a burden to him.*
Chizuru: "......"

*But since she had been trying not to slip and fall on the steps, her knees were a little weak by now.*
Satsuki: "...Phew."
*She exhaled and started walking again.*
*She stood at the entrance and rang the bell.*
Naori: "Hello― Oh, Sacchan?"
*Naori was the one who opened the door.*
Satsuki: "Hello. Umm, I've come for a physical today..."
Naori: "I see."
*Naori pointed to a door a short ways away.*
Naori: "That's the clinic entrance. This is our front door."
Satsuki: "Oh? Ah, I-I'm sorry..."
Naori: "Well, not like there's much difference. Oh, and it's not locked, so don't worry about ringing the bell."
Satsuki: "I-I see... Sorry about that."
*She bowed her head to Naori and entered through the other door.*
So: "Ah, so you went to the house door instead of this one."
*So, the director, said with a laugh.*
*Satsuki sat on a stool feeling a little uncomfortable.*
*She was shy around sociable adults like him.*
*She'd prefer it if he just left her alone.*
So: "Nanako-kun, her chart?"
Nanako: "Here."
So: "Just a physical today, right? Well, don't worry, we won't do much."
*So informed her, perhaps sensing her nervousness.*
Nanako: "We do have some blood work scheduled today, however."
*Nanako said, handing the chart to So.*
So: "Ah, that's right. ...Though I'd prefer to do some _butt_ work."
Nanako: "Aah?!"
*Nanako suddenly shrieked.*
Nanako: "...Come on, Doctor, please be serious!"
So: "Your physicals are as simple as that, Nanako-kun."
*So must have done something, but Satsuki couldn't see it.*
Nanako: "Are you okay with shots?"
*Nanako asked her.*
Satsuki: "...Yes, I think so."
*She knew what a "shot" was, but had never had one before.*
*The thought of being poked with a needle was a little scary, though.*
So: "I'll leave it to you then, Nanako-kun."
Nanako: "Right."
*Nanako brought over the tools.*
Nanako: "May I see your arm?"
Satsuki: "Of course."
*She rolled up the sleeve of her kimono and stuck her arm out.*
*Pale skin seemingly untouched by the sun.*
*Thin arms bearing almost no muscle.*
*Nanako tied a rubber tube around her upper arm.*
Satsuki: "Ngh..."
*It was a little tight.*
Nanako: "This is how we make the veins stand out."
*Exactly as she'd said, Satsuki saw blue lines popping up on her arm.*
*The inside of her elbow was wiped with a dampened piece of cotton.*
*A slightly cold sensation.*
Nanako: "Now, relax."
*Nanako said, placing her left thumb on a vein.*
Satsuki: "O-Okay..."
*When Satsuki saw the fat needle attached to the syringe in her right hand, she had to look away.*
*She'd rather not see that stab her.*
Nanako: "Relax..."
*With Nanako's voice, she felt the needle pierce her skin.*
Satsuki: "Gh..."
*She gripped the edge of her chair.*
*Still, she tried her best to relax her arm.*
*If she moved her arm and the needle broke...*
*That was the sort of thing she feared.*
Nanako: "Okay, we've got it."
*Satsuki looked up when Nanako said so.*
Satsuki: "Ugh..."
*The syringe was filling with red liquid.*
*As Nanako slowly pulled back the plunger, Satsuki felt something leaving her body.*
*It was blood, of course... but she felt like something else was being drawn out with it.*
Nanako: "That should be enough."
*Nanako stopped filling the syringe and quickly removed the rubber tube, pushing some cotton onto the wound as she pulled the needle out.*
Nanako: "Apply some pressure for a little bit, okay?"
Satsuki: "O― Okay..."
*She held the cotton down as she had been told.*
Nanako: "Can you wait outside for a little bit until the bleeding stops?"
Satsuki: "Oh...? Outside...?"
Nanako: "Oh, not _outside_ outside, just in the living room outside this door."
Satsuki: "Oh... Okay."
*It was sunny, but a cold winter day all the same.*
*Relieved that she wasn't being asked to wait outside, Satsuki staggered a little as she left the examination room.*
Ayato: "Oh, Sacchan?"
Satsuki: "Ah... Rihito-san?"
*Ayato was in the living room.*
*He placed the book he had been reading on the table and tilted his head.*
Ayato: "Were you at the clinic?"
Satsuki: "Y-Yes... Umm, for a physical. ...And you, Rihito-san?"
Ayato: "I came to see Nao-chan. He went back to his room, though."
Satsuki: "I-I see..."
*She was too surprised to say much else.*
Ayato: "...Did you get a shot?"
Satsuki: "Oh, I had blood drawn..."
*She pushed her fingers onto the cotton.*
Ayato: "...Did Nanako-san's shot hurt?"
Satsuki: "Um, well, not really..."
*Thinking back on it, for such a fat needle, it really hadn't hurt much at all.*
Ayato: "When I get shots, it always hurts."
*Ayato grimaced.*
Ayato: "Maybe it's on purpose."
Satsuki: "...Do you make a fuss and get in trouble?"
Ayato: "Of... course not."
*He looked away.*
Satsuki: "Heheh... Maybe that's why it hurts."
*Satsuki couldn't help smiling.*
Ayato: "I told you, I don't do that!"
*Ayato got worked up and denied it.*
Satsuki: "Heheh..."
*Good.*
*Thanks to Ayato, the faint sense of unease she'd been feeling faded.*
Satsuki: "...So, Rihito-san."
Ayato: "What is it?"
Satsuki: "The other day... we, umm, made a promise, right?"
Ayato: "Huh...? About after the festival?"
Satsuki: "Yes, but... I won't be able to see you on the day of the festival, so before that..."
Ayato: "Before...?"
*Satsuki brought her lips right up to Ayato's ear.*
Satsuki: "Yes... On the last day of February, at the hideout..."
*Satsuki whispered, then pulled back.*
Ayato: "Sacchan...?"
Satsuki: "...Please don't tell anyone. ...I won't speak of it anymore either."
*She placed her finger on her lips.*
Ayato: "O-Okay..."
*Ayato nodded, though he looked uncertain.*
Satsuki: "...I know, let's decide on a password."
Ayato: "A password?"
Satsuki: "How about, if one of us says something, and the other answers with a password, we discuss things?"
Ayato: "That sounds like fun."
Satsuki: "Doesn't it? What do you think would be good?"
Ayato: "'Mountain' and 'river' would be too simple, huh?"
Satsuki: "It would be better if other people couldn't figure it out. Something just you and I can understand."
Ayato: "Let's see... Ah, how about one of us says, 'It's snowing again today,' and the other responds, 'But the sky's clear'?"
Satsuki: "Even if it's cloudy?"
Ayato: "Well, it wouldn't be a password otherwise, right?"
Satsuki: "What if it's summer?"
Ayato: "...I dunno."
Satsuki: "Heheh... Let's come up with a different one in summer."
*The door opened, and Nanako peeked into the living room.*
Nanako: "Satsuki-chan, are you ready?"
Satsuki: "Yes. ...Umm, has the bleeding stopped?"
Ayato: "It's been pretty long. If it hasn't stopped yet, that'd be pretty bad."
*Ayato said, so Satsuki timidly removed her hand from the wound.*
*The cotton was dark with blood and a red dot was left on her arm.*
Nanako: "Let's continue the examination."
*Nanako suggested.*
Satsuki: "Alright. ...Well, see you, Rihito-san."
Ayato: "Yeah."

*A room with a wooden floor inside the Shigusa Shrine.*
*Karen sat on the floor with Yu and Meguri.*
Yuka: "Excuse me, Young Miss."
*Yuka and Miya brought in a large basin.*
*They left it on top of a woven mat in front of Karen and her friends.*
*Inside the basin was the clay she and her brother had been kneading the other day.*
*Yuka sat down behind Karen.*
Miya: "Is everything ready?"
*Miya looked around at the four seated on the floor.*
Meguri: "Umm, what exactly are we doing?"
*Meguri raised her hand, not quite grasping the situation.*
Miya: "Preparing for the festival. You'll be making some decorative items."
*Miya took out some colorful paper and handed it to Meguri and Yu.*
Yu: "What's this?"
Miya: "Can you make _yakko-san_ and cranes?"
Meguri: "That'll be easy enough."
Miya: "I'll leave it to you, then."
Karen: "Umm, what should I―"
Miya: "You kneaded this clay already, right, Karen-san?"
Karen: "Yes... with my brother."
Miya: "You'll continue from where you left off last time. Just form a certain shape with the clay."
Karen: "Understood."
*Yuka placed a bucket full of water next to her.*
Yuka: "I'll lend a hand."
Karen: "Sure, I appreciate it."
*She dipped her hands in the cold water. After shaking some of it off, she moved her hands to the clay.*
Karen: "How big should it be?"
*She asked Miya.*
Miya: "Let's see... It says '6 to 7 sun,' so about 20 centimeters?"
*Miya said, looking at an old book.*
Miya: "Use this as a reference for the shape."
*She handed the book to Yuka, who held the page open and showed it to Karen.*
*The shape looked like a cicada nymph with a rounded back.*
*The only part that made it look human was its head, which was clearly separate from its body.*
*It had arms and legs too, but they were short and didn't seem to serve much purpose.*
*It was almost like a caterpillar...*
Karen: "What is this...?"
*She asked Miya.*
Miya: "It's nothing."
*It couldn't be "nothing," of course, but that was Miya's answer.*
Karen: "Umm, this looks sort of difficult... I'm not very confident I'll be able to recreate it well..."
Miya: "It doesn't need to be perfect. Just try for a similar shape."
Karen: "Is that so?"
*It should be expected to be well-made, she figured, if it was going to be used for the festival.*
Miya: "Well, I'll leave it to you."
*Miya left the room with a bow.*
Meguri: "...Ohina, what is it?"
*Meguri glanced over, an origami crane in her hand.*
Karen: "...I'm not really sure."
Yu: "So you're making something else, then. ...What is this?"
*Yu murmured, looking at the book Yuka was holding.*
Karen: "Don't ask me..."
Yuka: "Umm... I'm not sure, but do you think this could be... Hinna-sama, perhaps?"
*Yuka said, timidly.*
Meguri: "Hinna-sama... The thing displayed in Ohina's house?"
Karen: "It's inside the household shrine, so I've never seen it..."
*Supposedly, Hinna-sama brought fortune to those who worshipped it.*
*The Hinagami family were the only ones in the settlement allowed to worship it.*
Yu: "And you're making a new one?"
Karen: "But... is it really okay for me to make it?"
Meguri: "Well, you're a Hinagami, so it should be fine, right?"
*Of course, there was no way for these girls to know if they were right.*
Yuka: "But... I've heard that if you worship it in the wrong way, you'll be cursed."
*Karen froze just as she was about to touch the clay.*
Karen: "...N-Nothing so unscientific as 'curses' would actually exist, right?"
Yu: "...Ohina, your voice is shaking."
Karen: "And anyway! If the problem is with the worshipping, then the _making_ shouldn't have anything to do with it, right?!"
Meguri: "Hopefully."
*Meguri launched a paper airplane made with the origami paper.*
Yuka: "...It was over a decade ago, but I hear the curse has actually happened before."
Yu: "I've heard the same thing. It was long enough ago that we may not have even been born yet, right?"
Meguri: "...So who died?"
Yu: "I don't know the details. My grandma won't talk about it, after all."
Karen: "Well, I'm not doing any worshipping or anything, so I won't be cursed!"
*Karen shouted and grabbed the clay, beginning to knead it.*
*Without a moment's delay, Yuka placed a wooden board beneath her hands.*
*She used her body weight to soften the clay.*
*She was able to shape it easily, perhaps because it had been kneaded once before already.*
Karen: "Please show me the shape, Yuka-san."
Yuka: "Yes, Young Miss."
*Yuka held the book up so that Karen could see it easily.*
Karen: "Hmm... Like this?"
*Karen piled the clay on the wooden board in a crescent and formed it into a basic shape.*
Yuka: "Do you need the spatula?"
Karen: "Yes, if you would."
*She took the spatula from Yuka and started scraping the clay away, forming the legs.*
Meguri: "...Is it a chicken wing?"
Karen: "No, it's not!"
Meguri: "But... well..."
Yu: "It doesn't look quite like the picture."
*Meguri and Yu exchanged glances.*
Karen: "I'm not finished yet!"
*Karen decided to ignore her and immerse herself in her creation.*
*She silently scraped away the earth, forming the shape.*
*The other two seemed to be concentrating on their origami as well.*
*Completed origami figures lined up around Meguri and Yu.*
*Things like cranes, _Hina_ dolls, and even _temari_.*
Meguri: "Young Mistress, can you make a goldfish?"
Yu: "It's the same as a helmet in the beginning, so..."
*Yu started folding.*
*Karen glanced over.*
Yuka: "Come on, Young Miss."
*Yuka prompted her when her hands stopped moving.*
Karen: "Right..."
*Karen wished she were doing origami too.*
*_Why do I have to make this creepy thing?_*
*If only her brother were here too...*
Yuka: "Young Miss...?"
Karen: "...Pardon me, I have to use the restroom..."
*Karen stood and left the room.*
*There was no bathroom in the hall of worship, so Karen left the building and headed toward the shrine office.*
*She walked toward the rear of the office to use the back door... then stopped.*
Karen: "Father...?"
*Shizuru was there.*
Shizuru: "...Please do so."
*He was talking to someone.*
*Karen hid in the shadow of the building and watched him quietly.*
Saya: "Yes, I will."
*It was Saya.*
*The mood between them was intimate, and Karen felt as though she was witnessing something she shouldn't.*
Saya: "What a sinful gentleman you are."
*Saya's voice sounded provocative.*
Shizuru: "I couldn't run a company without being aware of that."
Saya: "Heheh..."
Karen: "Eek?!"
*Karen yelped in surprise when a gob of snow suddenly dropped down right next to her from the roof.*
Shizuru: "―Gh?!"
*Shizuru ran over when he heard her voice.*
Shizuru: "...Karen, huh?"
Karen: "Ah... F-Father...?"
*His expression was more frightening than she'd ever seen before.*
*But it was only for an instant.*
Shizuru: "...Can you stand?"
*When he reached down to Karen where she sat, his face was already back to normal.*
Karen: "Y-Yes... Why are you here, Father...?"
Shizuru: "...For a meeting about the festival."
*Saya had already disappeared.*
*Maybe she'd gone in through the back door.*
Karen: "I-I see..."
*She had no way to refute that excuse, even if Shizuru had never once expressed an interest in the festival in several years.*
Shizuru: "...Don't tell anyone what you just saw. Okay?"
Karen: "Huh...? O-Okay..."
*Her father's expression was no different than normal.*
*Shizuru brushed the snow off of Karen's clothes and walked off.*
Karen: "Father..."
*What was he talking to Saya about?*
*What was he doing with Saya?*
*Her curiosity was limitless, but she couldn't tell anyone about this.*
*Shizuru was bereaved of Karen's mother.*
*Saya was unmarried.*
*_There should be no problem_... Did Karen think so because she was mature for her age?*

====================02b_0800.txt====================
*Inside the storehouse.*
*Satsuki was fixing her collar in front of the mirror.*
*Her lips were faintly tinged red.*
*There was a little makeup around her eyes, too.*
*"You seem to be having fun."*
*Her mouth formed the words.*
*"You may be right."*
*The same mouth answered.*
*The calendar on the wall showed that it was the last day of February.*
*Today was the day of her promise.*
*She stood and fixed the hem of her skirt.*
*_Good._*
*She'd gone to the trouble of arranging to meet on a different day, so she didn't want anyone interfering with her plans.*
*Satsuki quietly opened the door of the storehouse.*
*No one was outside.*
*She left the building.*
*It wasn't snowing.*
*She walked across the trampled snow in her sandals.*
*The faint sound of a drum could be heard from inside the shrine office.*
*It was probably in preparation for the festival.*
*The shrine grounds.*
*There was a pile of lumber clean of snow, perhaps for use in the festival.*
*She heard there would be stands, albeit modest ones.*
*There would also be a stage in front of the hall of worship.*
*There, the Miko would offer her dance―the main purpose of the festival.*
*She descended the stairs toward Kamihinna.*
Ayato: "Ah..."
Satsuki: "Oh?"
*Ayato was at the crossroads.*
*He carried a paper bag in his hands.*
Ayato: "I bought some candy―caramels and _mizuame_."
Satsuki: "Wow..."
*She peeked inside the bag.*
*There was a red box of caramels and a bottle inside.*
Ayato: "Well, shall we go, Sacchan?"
Satsuki: "Let's."
*The two walked side-by-side toward Hidarihinna.*
Ayato: "―And then old man Saizo yelled at me for wasting my money on sweets."
*They chatted as they climbed the hill.*
Ayato: "'Wasting your time fooling around when the country's in this state?!' But that's got nothing to do with us yet, right?"
Satsuki: "You're right."
*Satsuki agreed.*
Ayato: "But he'd have just lectured me again if I tried to say anything, so I apologized and ran off."
*Ayato put his hand on the door of the hideout.*
Ayato: "Huh...? It won't open."
Satsuki: "There's snow packed into the frame."
*Satsuki pointed to the bottom of the door.*
*Snow had been blown into the door by the wind.*
Ayato: "You're right. Hold this for a second."
*Handing the paper bag to Satsuki, Ayato crouched down and scraped at the snow.*
Ayato: "Ack, it's frozen."
Satsuki: "Umm, you could try using this..."
*She picked up a pointed shovel that was leaning against the wall.*
*Its tip, which had been buried in the snow, had ice on it too.*
Ayato: "Thanks."
*Ayato hit the ice with the tip of the shovel.*
*Shards of ice flew about.*
Ayato: "Just a bit more."
*Satsuki slid the door.*
*It creaked noisily and opened just a little.*
Ayato: "Keep moving it, would you?"
Satsuki: "Ah, sure."
*The ice stuck to the door frame was scraped away.*
*Finally it opened wide enough for one person to pass through.*
Ayato: "After you."
Satsuki: "Alright."
*She turned sideways, holding the paper bag, and entered.*
*Ayato took his scarf off and opened the windows for ventilation.*
Ayato: "First things first, we should start a fire."
*He fished some matches out of the paper bag.*
*Satsuki scraped out the remaining charcoal from the ash in the _hibachi_.*
*They lit some newspapers and placed the charcoal on top.*
Satsuki: "This will... take some time."
Ayato: "If you're cold, you could get in the _futon_ over there."
Satsuki: "What?"
*She turned around.*
*The _futon_ was still sitting on top of the _tatami_.*
*It was the one the Young Mistress―Futami Yu―had brought.*
Ayato: "Oh... Your kimono might get wrinkled."
Satsuki: "...I don't mind that, but... aren't you cold too, Rihito-san?"
Ayato: "I'm fine."
*Ayato said, watching the _hibachi_.*
Satsuki: "But..."
*Satsuki couldn't help thinking Ayato was just trying to act tough.*

====================02c_0200.txt====================
*Deep in the night, when all were asleep, a group walked down the road.*
*Because of the falling snow, it was not truly dark.*
*Yet the group was enveloped in darkness and appeared to glide over their surroundings―but no, their feet touched the snowy ground.*
*No one existed to question them.*
*They seemed to glide down the road to a particular house.*
*The door opened soundlessly and they entered.*
*It was a normal residence.*
*The owner of the house was in bed.*
*She must have been sleeping deeply, for even with the intruders by her pillow, she did not wake.*
*Perhaps there was another reason she did not awaken.*
*Incense burned inside the room.*
*Black robes swept away the smoke.*
*Yet the woman still did not wake.*
*One of them wielded a dagger.*
*Its blade quivered.*
*The entire black robe quivered.*
*The dagger almost fell several times before its wielder settled on a reverse grip.*
*The blade pointed down at the woman's stomach.*
*Still, it trembled.*
*Another hand grabbed the one holding the blade.*
*It seemed to push the blade down as the other hand resisted.*
*The head under the black robes shook back and forth.*
*But... as if giving in, the head dropped and the dagger rose.*
*The dagger was brought down with the wielder's body weight.*
*The blade sunk into the woman's stomach.*
"Ghh―!"
*The woman groaned.*
*Her mouth was quickly covered.*
*The dagger was pulled out.*
*Fresh blood spilled from the wound.*
*The futon was dyed red.*
*The dagger swung downward.*
*Again and again.*
*Blood splattered everywhere, yet the blade continued to fall again and again.*
*The woman's body eventually stopped jumping and grew still.*
*The black robes rested for a moment.*
*The woman didn't twitch anymore.*
*Life seemed to have left her body.*
*But there was still work to do.*
*The dagger rose again and plunged into her abdomen.*
*The now limp flesh was sliced open.*
*Blood and entrails spilled from her open stomach.*
*White and black and red mixed together and began to stain everything in a blended color.*
*No one could see the particulars in the darkness.*
*If they could... they would not be able to maintain their sanity.*
*A lump of dirt with a gnarled shape was placed on the floor.*
*The same shape as the lump of clay the Miko had crumbled in the festival earlier.*
*A hand from the black robe took it.*
*It was shoved into the woman's open stomach.*
*The clay was immediately stained red with blood.*
*The entrails in the way were pulled out and severed.*
*Filth spouted out like water and dirtied the area.*
*The hands were forced to stop their work.*
*A sour smell spread throughout the room.*
*An unbearable stench.*
*A stench foul enough to make eyes water.*
*Or rather... perhaps the situation itself had produced the tears.*
*But it had to be seen through to the end.*
*That was what fate had decided.*
