====================03a_1209_05.txt====================
*After dinner, I lie around in my room, documents in one hand.*
*It's stuff about the clay dolls we found inside the victims' stomachs.*
*The dirt was red clay, found anywhere in the Kanto region, and there weren't any hand prints or the like on them.*
*It's hard to imagine there are clay dolls in the form of fetuses being sold as art or something anywhere.*
*Meaning... these dolls were made for this specific purpose.*
*They were about 20 centimeters long―four or five months into gestation if they had been real fetuses.*
*Since the stomach was cut open and sewed back up instead of growing slowly like an actual pregnancy, this is probably the biggest it could be and still fit inside.*
*But what does it mean...? That the victims were pregnant?*
*Or were the clay dolls stuffed inside to hide the fact that they were pregnant?*
*...No, of course not.*
*Kamizono Mayu's uterus was heavily damaged, but the clay doll was stuffed in outside of her womb.*
*I gaze at the autopsies Natsume-san compiled for Kamizono Mayu and Itose Mizuki.*
*There was no evidence of sexual intercourse on Kamizono Mayu's body.*
*Itose Mizuki's uterus showed no signs of pregnancy.*
*These things are clear no matter what camouflage the perpetrator attempted.*
*Should I be looking at the clay dolls as components of some sort of ritual after all?*
*But... I've never heard of such a ritual.*
*I enter the library.*
*There are several customs involving clay dolls all around the country dating from the Edo period.*
*They seem to tie mostly to faith in the Fushimi Inari, but they also usually seem to be colored and sold as souvenirs.*
*For these dolls that seem to be used in rituals... they may be closer to something like clay figures.*
*If that's the case, I'd have to look even further back, to the Jomon period.*
*Is there anything like that in a more modern type of indigenous faith?*
*...Though I can't imagine that a ceremony in which a woman's stomach is cut open and a clay doll is stuffed inside would be left behind in writing.*
*Maybe a similar ceremony is being twisted into these murders.*
*...Is this where the Blessed Congregation comes into things?*
*There's no evidence of that.*
*But I think it's worth looking into.*
*I'll ask Toji to check it out.*
*She knows a little more than I do about the Blessed Congregation.*
*The question is whether the Blessed Congregation―or Senri, rather―used anything like a clay doll in their rituals.*
*It's a little painful that this is all deduction, though.*
*I'll look into Kamizono Mayu, like I had planned in the first place.*
*...And Masaki Tomoyuki.*
*I don't think it'll be long until he's out of the hospital.*
*It's fine with him presently in the hospital, but I can't guarantee he won't disappear when he's discharged.*
*...I wouldn't feel great about letting him die out on the street somewhere.*
*There's a very low chance that he's the culprit.*
*...Low, but not zero.*
*I'm well aware of that fact, since I was the one who proved his innocence.*
*...Guess I'll have to keep an eye on him.*

*Satsuki was dead. There was a police investigation in the settlement for a little while, but I never learned anything.*
*The investigation ended with everything still in the dark and Satsuki was buried somewhere in Kakurehinna; I wasn't even allowed to visit her grave.*
*I wasted my time, unable to motivate myself to do anything with my life. Then the war started. I was the eldest son and had no military obligation, but I enlisted right away.*
*It wasn't out of any respectable reason, like "for my country." I was simply looking for a place to die.*
*After training I was immediately sent over to the mainland. After that I wandered from Malay to Java to Sumatra.*
*What I learned there... was that people die very easily. By tiny bullets, or simple traps, or even being bitten by a mosquito or a centipede...*
*I saw people marching alongside me have their heads burst open like pomegranates. I abandoned people who'd been shot in the leg and couldn't move.*
*There were no simple platitudes there. You wouldn't survive if you met an enemy and couldn't kill them on the spot. And I held a weapon that killed people easily.*
*My senses were completely numb. I got used to death. I got used to killing.*
*I thought I would get used to the concept of Satsuki's death at some point too. But she appeared in my dreams when I slept. Every night, Satsuki was in my dreams, dead.*
*Dead in every way possible. The corpses I saw on the battlefield all came back to me as Satsuki. I woke up every day covered in corpses of Satsuki.*
*One night when I was on sentry duty in the Philippines, I asked the man next to me if he dreamed. He was a few years older than me... and named Masaki.*
*He said the enemy soldiers he killed appeared in his dreams too. But he laughed, saying they didn't show up on nights when he'd eaten his fill.*
*There weren't many provisions deep in the jungle with us, and the supply lines were often cut off. Even before opening hostilities, many of my comrades starved to death.*
*I talked to him often. About the country in Nagano; I grew up in the country too, so we had a lot in common. But he was unlike me in that he had no relatives.*
*He grew ill and collapsed on the front as well. He was ravaged by high fevers from malaria, and we had no medicine. There was no way for him to recover in his state of malnutrition.*
*He was buried there, with the other casualties. He left nothing behind to give to anyone, and had no one to give anything to.*
*The New Year came and the US forces landed on the island. We resisted, terrified of their bombardments and tanks. They bulldozed paths deep into the mountains and invaded.*
*We starving soldiers had no way to resist them. We collapsed one by one and our forces dwindled before my eyes.*
*I realized that I was the only member of my unit left alive. I was taken in by another unit and the fighting continued... until the war finally ended.*
*I was lucky to be relatively close to the main force when the ceasefire order was handed down. I went back home without having to waste my life dying after the war was already over.*
*That's right... I thought I was lucky to have survived. Even though I had lost my will to live after Satsuki's death and had been searching for a place to die.*
*I realized that on the train back to Toyama. I was returning to my hometown with no doubts in my mind.*
*I believed it was Satsuki who kept me alive. I returned to the Hitogata Settlement to take revenge for Satsuki.*
*As I gazed at the nostalgic scenery of Omotehinna... I decided to find Satsuki's killer.*

*There was one thing he hadn't asked at the shrine.*
*...It was about the Miko.*
*Apparently the Miko hadn't danced at the festival since that incident.*
*That gave a sense of realism to his theory that Satsuki had been the Miko.*
*But during that last festival... when the Miko was dancing, Ayato had been with Satsuki.*
*The Miko on the stage, however, was wearing a mask and he had been unable to see her face.*
*Then... had someone switched places with the Miko at that time?*
*...But that would have been strange too.*
*The Miko's purpose was to dance at the festival.*
*It didn't make sense for someone else to do it when the Miko was present.*
*But... on the other hand, if that wasn't the case, it still didn't make sense.*
*The more he thought about the theory that Satsuki was the Miko, the further it fell apart.*
*But that was all that he could think.*
*Satsuki had been the Miko, and someone else had offered the dance...*
*If that was the case, then who had danced?*
*He couldn't tell very well on the stage, but the dancing figure had seemed of a like stature to Satsuki.*
*If so, then it couldn't have been a man.*
*Satsuki's height... Yu and Nanako were tall for women, and Yuka was too short.*
*...Now that he thought about it, Nanako wasn't at the festival that day.*
*Did that fact carry any significance...?*
*As for the other people it could have been? Those who knew the dance.*
*Saya was the only person he knew of.*
*She had always offered the dance as the Miko's representative.*
*She would definitely have been able to fill in for her.*
*But she had been on stage with the Miko during the offering, playing the flute.*
*It was impossible for her to have filled in that day.*
*Saya's sister―Kensei's wife, Miya―had been on stage as well, guiding the Miko.*
*She wouldn't have been able to fill in either.*
*What about Yoshimitsu's wife, Rioko...? He honestly didn't know.*
*He hadn't seen her during the festival, and she wasn't the type to leave the house very often, at any rate.*
*She was Ayato's great-aunt, who had married into the Shigusa family from the Hinagami family.*
Yuka: "Ayato-sama, please sit up so I can change your bandages."
Ayato: "Mm, okay..."
*He sat up and crossed his legs on the _futon_ at Yuka's prompt.*
Yuka: "Please excuse me."
*Yuka reached around Ayato's stomach and started unwrapping his bandages.*
Ayato: "...Hey, Yuka-san?"
Yuka: "Yes?"
*Yuka responded without pause in her task.*
Ayato: "The Miko hasn't appeared at the festival since that incident, right?"
*Yuka's hands stopped.*
Yuka: "...Right. That's what I've heard."
Ayato: "We don't see the Miko except at the festival―I wonder what she does other than that."
Yuka: "Hard to say... She's a messenger of the gods, so I hadn't thought about it."
*...That was probably common sense among the people of Hitogata.*
Karen: "Yuka!"
Yuka: "Oh, Young Miss..."
Karen: "Wh-What is this improper―?! Undressing him on top of the _futon_ like this!"
Ayato: "...Erm, Karen, she's just cleaning my back."
Karen: "I-I know, but―! I-It's imprudent!"
*Karen grabbed Yuka's arm and pulled her up.*
Karen: "I said _I_ would take care of my brother, did I not?"
Yuka: "I-I'm terribly sorry... but you seemed busy with your dance practice, Young Miss, so I―"
Karen: "Whatever, just come here!"
*Karen pulled Yuka out of the room.*
*His bandages were half-wrapped.*
*Cold air from the hallway blew in from the open door.*
*Bending forward and closing the door, he re-wrapped his own bandages and lay down on the _futon_.*
Ayato: "Hahh..."
*He stared at his hands for no particular reason.*
*His skin was darkened from the sun and the dirt of the jungle.*
*His fingers were thin from hunger and thirst.*
*He wondered how long it would take for them to return to normal.*
*...He thought about the parts missing from Satsuki's body.*
*She had lost her limbs.*
*What could that have meant...?*
*It was different from the curse.*
*The Miko, messenger of Hinna-sama, would never be cursed.*
*Was it necessary for the culprit to have taken her arms and legs?*
*What reason could there have been for that...?*
*The police had been identifying people with their fingerprints since the Meiji era.*
*Were Satsuki's limbs severed to prevent her fingerprints from being taken...?*
*That seemed like flimsy reasoning, though.*
*The corpse had immediately been identified as Satsuki, and no one knew where she was from anyway, so her fingerprints would have been useless.*
*And if they didn't want her fingerprints taken, all they had to do was sever her fingers.*
*Satsuki's arms may have been slender, but that would have been far more efficient.*
Ayato: "...I don't get it."
*There must have been some reason, but Ayato had no idea what it could be.*

====================04b_0100.txt====================
*Ayato was cooped up in his room the next day with the excuse that it was to let his wounds heal.*
*Documents he'd taken out from their cellar were stacked up next to his pillow.*
*Most of them had to do with the Miko.*
*He started reading about the birthplace of the Miko.*
*The records showed that they were usually from the Hitogata Settlement―in the past, Hitogata Village.*
*From the warring states to the Edo period, this area was part of the Kaga domain under the Maeda clan.*
*Some Shigusa who was chief vassal to the Maeda family was exiled here, attended by some Hinagami, and the two of them founded the village, or so the records said.*
*The Shigusa established the shrine and the Hinagami became headman and governed the village.*
*The two families had supported the growth of Hitogata Village since then.*
*The Miko... apparently showed up suddenly at the end of the Edo period.*
*It was written that the Miko descended from heaven, exactly as the name implied.*
*This part was something like folklore or mythology.*
*That is to say... there was nothing credible about this information.*
*It must have been true that someone known as the Miko appeared back then, but they hadn't kept records of where she'd come from―whether it had been outside of the village or otherwise.*
*They'd probably kept her origins a secret on purpose... perhaps to heighten her mystique.*
*There was also a description of Hinna-sama.*
*It was a doll god that only the Hinagami family could worship.*
*It had been created with soil from the village and was enshrined and worshipped in March, bestowing fortune on the village.*
*It was said that Hinna-sama would grant any wish.*
*...But only if worshipped properly.*
*Only the Hinagami family had been told the proper way to worship the god, and if someone else worshipped a fake god with different methods, they would be possessed and killed by Hinna-sama.*
*That was Hinna-sama's Curse.*
*He figured out that much with just a quick glance.*
*The Miko and Hinna-sama were written about separately.*
*Going from the order of the records, the Miko had appeared for the purpose of worshipping Hinna-sama.*
*He wanted more detailed information about the Miko―more recent information.*
*Ayato searched through more records.*
*He found a book with plain binding, like a diary.*
*The paper cover looked relatively new as well.*
*It was filled with concise sentences.*
*1897, Miko manifests. Dance offered.*
*1898 to 1902, dances offered.*
*1903, dance offered. Miko returns to heaven.*
*1921, Miko manifests. Dance offered.*
*1922 and 23, dances offered.*
*1924, dance offered. Miko returns to heaven.*
*It must have been a record of appearances of past Miko.*
*Between these... and the last two times, there had been a gap of 20 or so years.*
*It looked as if every time a Miko appeared, she would offer the dance at the festival for a few years afterward.*
*For the years without a Miko, someone like Saya probably stood in for her.*
*A Miko appeared in Meiji, in Taisho, and in Showa.*
*If it had been the same person...*
*He had no doubt that the Miko was human.*
*Ayato didn't believe that something supernatural could actually appear.*
*There must have been a reason for one to appear every 20 years or so...*
Ayato: "...I have no idea."
*He set the book back down.*
*Ayato never was good at critical thinking, so he was simply laying out the facts.*
*He picked up another book.*
*It looked like a copy of a shrine offering record.*
*It had records of offerings of either _tamagushi_ or fees for them every year during March.*
*It made sense for the Hinagami family to have them as something like a representative for the shrine's parishioners.*
*It didn't look like it would have any clues about the Miko, either.*
*There were other occurrences the books he brought up from the cellar said nothing about.*
*...Such as the curse.*
*Before the war, the night of the festival just before Satsuki died...*
*A woman named Kawase Sachiko had died and the people of the settlement had feared it as the curse.*
*Ayato had no idea how she had been killed.*
*But he felt that it could have been referred to as such because there was a precedent for the curse.*
*That book earlier had described Hinna-sama's Curse.*
*Kawase Sachiko had been cursed and had died for worshipping a fake Hinna-sama... That was how the story went, anyway.*
*He had no idea whether or not that was true, of course.*
*In any case, there were no records of examples of the curse in any of the books from the cellar.*
*Perhaps records weren't left about it because it was so abominable.*
Ayato: "...Phew."
*With a sigh, he stood up.*
*The new skin on his back felt stiff.*
*He wouldn't make any progress having a staring contest with these books.*
*He'd have to go to the shrine and ask more questions.*
*They, of all people, might have had more records.*

====================04b_0110.txt====================
*He climbed the long stone steps and arrived at the Shigusa Shrine.*
*There was no one to be seen and the grounds were dead silent.*
*If he was going to ask questions, Kensei would probably be the one to talk to.*
*Was he in the shrine?*
*Ayato headed in that direction.*

Ayato: "It's been a while."

====================04b_0200.txt====================
*Behind the shrine office...*
*An old storehouse towered.*
*Snow was piled up around it and there was no way to get to it without leaving footprints.*
*Having no choice, he stepped onto the snow.*
*This storehouse was where Satsuki had lived.*
*That was what the documents at the police station stated.*
*He wanted to find something that he couldn't from the pictures alone.*
*...Though with the months and years that had passed since then, it was much less likely that he'd find anything.*
*But Ayato still wanted to find some trace of Satsuki.*
*There were fittings for a large padlock on the outside of the door.*
*But there was no lock.*
*...It was open.*
*Either they had never locked it in the first place, or they hadn't put the lock on since there was nothing inside... He wouldn't know until he saw for himself.*
*Making sure no one was coming from the shrine office, Ayato slipped into the storehouse.*
*The sun was still high in the sky, but the light was dim inside the storehouse.*
*Turning the light on, he looked around inside.*
*Dust had accumulated on the floor.*
*Probably as much as the snow outside.*
*He doubted anyone had been in here in a long time. There were no footprints in the dust; it looked completely undisturbed.*
*The only movement was the fluttering of dust above the dirt floor.*
*There was nothing here... No, there was a large chest in the corner.*
*Other than that, the only other thing in the room was a full-length mirror.*
*It was supposed to be a storage shed, yet there was nothing in it.*
*No traces of Satsuki having lived here, either...*
*Had everything been disposed of?*
*He crouched down and examined the dusty floor.*
*He held his breath so that he didn't breathe any of it in.*
*There looked to be a squarish area where the floor was sunk down next to the wall.*
*He wiped some dust from the floor near the entrance.*
*Faded floorboards appeared.*
*Had there been something there for a long enough time to make the floor sink like that?*
*Resolving himself, he stepped up onto the floor in his shoes.*
*Dust scattered into the air with every step he took.*
*Ayato arrived at the wall in the back, feeling like he was about to have a coughing fit.*
*He knelt down again and swept the dust away from the floor.*
*The floor was a different color where the dent was.*
*Both colors were faded, but the dented floor was a little darker.*
*It looked as if something used to be here after all.*
*He stood and checked the size of the dented area.*
*It must have been a dresser or something large like that.*
*Now that he looked closer, he noticed other depressions along the wall.*
*Since there weren't any in the middle of the room, it must have been furniture.*
*It looked like Satsuki had been living here after all, as per the police data.*
*But... what could be the reason they had to clean it so thoroughly?*
*He would understand if they had cleaned it up and turned it into storage again.*
*But it didn't make sense to clean it up and claim that Satsuki had lived there.*
*Were they unable to feign innocence? Or did the investigation find that out?*
*He couldn't tell, even though he'd seen the documents.*
*There was another thing that had been bothering him since he'd entered this storehouse...*
*Ayato looked down at the chest in the corner.*
*Perhaps due to its age, its lock was coming loose and was secured with string.*
*He had no expectations about its contents... but why had this alone been left in the storehouse?*
*He discovered the answer right away.*
*It was attached to the wall and floor.*
*It wasn't a container meant to be moved around, but rather built into the building.*
*He tried to move the chest to test that theory, and it didn't budge.*
*The clasp broke off and fell to the floor.*
*Before picking it up, Ayato laid his hand on the lid.*
*The hinge along the wall creaked as the lid opened.*
*And just as Ayato had expected... it was empty.*
*Maybe a _futon_ or clothes had been kept in it, as there were some fibers on the bottom.*
*The light hit the inside of the chest.*
*He bent himself forward, looked inside and found a small hole where a wood knot had once been.*
*...It was like a peephole.*
*He opened the lid wide and stepped inside.*
*The floor gave a loud creak.*
*The inside of the chest was very cold.*
*It was too cramped for his adult body to fit inside the box and see through the peephole.*
*But if he were smaller... he would fit inside this chest.*
Ayato: "Hmm...? What's this...?"
*Around the hole...*
*There were many small, inconspicuous scratches.*
Ayato: "'A'... 'ya'... 'to'? No―'ko'...?"
*..."Ayako."*
*Was it someone's name?*
*He ran through different characters for the name in his mind...*
*It was all the more curious for him because his own name was Ayato.*
*Had Satsuki carved this?*
*Or...*
*He stood and got out of the chest.*
*Had there been someone named Ayako here?*
*There was also the possibility that it was Satsuki herself.*
*Or that it was from a different time period. The possibilities were endless once he started considering them.*
*At the very least, he was sure that he didn't know anyone named Ayako.*
*He closed the lid and returned the clasp to its place.*
*There were footprints all over the floor.*
*There would be nothing he could do to get out of it if he were discovered.*
*_Maybe I should just sweep the whole thing..._*
*He thought, but that would have taken far too much time.*
*He brushed away as much as he could so that his footprints didn't stand out and approached the mirror in doing so.*
*It wasn't being maintained and had become rather dull.*
*It was fairly useless now as a mirror.*
*He opened the drawers in the stand, but nothing was inside them.*
*It couldn't really be called a clue, but the fact that a mirror was in here could have been evidence that a woman lived here.*
*That, and the name "Ayako" etched into the chest.*
*He might have to look into that.*
*Ayato wiped off more of his footprints and stepped down to the dirt floor.*
*The dense dust in the air reflected the light shining in from the window.*
*He would start having lung problems if he stayed here much longer.*
*He headed outside and closed the door.*
*Ayato left the area, brushing his footprints out of the snow as he went.*

*Perhaps he needed to find one point to focus on.*
*If he found out who Satsuki really was, he might find out why she was killed.*
*And if he knew why she was killed, he might be able to figure out who killed her.*
*He knew he was being too optimistic, but that was all he could think for the time being.*
*In that case, the books by his pillow probably wouldn't do him any good.*
*He would have to guess some degree of Satsuki's background and try to find the rest of it from there.*
*First... Satsuki's birth.*
*Kensei had said that she was entrusted to them by an acquaintance of Yoshimitsu.*
*But from Kensei's tone at the time, that seemed like a lie.*
*A lie to hide where she had truly been born.*
*When he considered why they would need to hide it... a possibility came to his mind.*
*The possibility that Satsuki was born in secret here in this village.*
*If no record of her birth was sent out and the Shigusa family hid her existence...*
*Of course, there were some unreasonable aspects of this theory.*
*Why would she have to be hidden for over ten years after she was born?*
*And why would she be revealed in that winter?*
*Ayato was about the same age as Satsuki.*
*Maybe something happened in this village around the time he was born―at the end of the Taisho period.*
*Perhaps a family was murdered and left behind a single child...*
*These were nothing more than Ayato's wild theories, however.*
*He didn't think there was any reason or worth in investigating them...*
*But there were only a few people he could ask about that time period.*
Ayato: "...The branch office should have old newspapers."
*Naori had told him that once in the past.*
*Of course, that was before the war, so he had no idea if they would still be there.*
*But he decided to go tomorrow.*
*For tonight... he should sleep.*

====================04b_0400.txt====================

*His mother died in winter, 1929... March, he believed.*
*A newspaper from March, 1929... the morning paper on the 6th, in the lower left.*

*There weren't any incidents.*

*Either way, Saizo didn't seem likely to say more on this subject.*

Saizo: "...Here are the clippings from the end of Taisho to the beginning of Showa."
*Saizo handed Ayato a scrapbook of clippings.*
*He leafed through it.*
*There weren't many, because it was only articles that had to do with the Hitogata Settlement―still Hitogata Village at the time.*
*The achievements of Hinagami Pharmaceuticals, festivals at the Shigusa Shrine, the installation of telephones and electricity...*
*There was nothing that seemed like it would have anything to do with Satsuki.*
*There was nothing about the curse either, of course.*
*He had no idea whether it was never written about in the paper in the first place or whether those particular clippings were purposely not kept.*
*But there was no way for him to investigate things like this.*

*It was about past incidents of the curse.*
*It was the first time he had found an example of the curse before Kawase Sachiko's case.*
*And his mother had committed suicide the very next day.*
*What had happened on that day...?*
*It had nothing to do with Satsuki.*
*However... he couldn't ignore it.*

====================04b_0500.txt====================

*Inui's eyes stared at Ayato's.*

*Inui sipped tea from a teacup.*

Ayato: "...I believe all of the incidents were committed by human hands."
*He managed to squeeze that out.*

Inui: "That's all I can think of. ...She was asking him for a lot of money, apparently. Zaizen Keiko lived in poverty."
Ayato: "...Is that all?"
Inui: "I know that Hinagami Shizuru had his hands on a lot of women. Though that's not something I should be telling his son."
Ayato: "...It's got nothing to do with me."
*It didn't concern Ayato what his father did, nor where.*

Inui: "No, none ever surfaced. ...After all, Shigusa Saya was the one who discovered both Zaizen Keiko's and Hinagami Rika's bodies."

Ayato: "...Do you mean to say that Saya-san covered up all of the evidence?"

*Inui brought his tea to his lips.*

Inui: "I can't tell you that. It's an important lead, after all."
Ayato: "I see... Is it something that points to the Shigusa family, then?"
Inui: "It wouldn't be unusual. All of the previous victims of the curse were people who were inconvenient for the two families."
Ayato: "...Then why did my mother commit suicide?"
*Ayato ended up asking him about his mother after all.*
Inui: "Because she learned of her husband's deeds, perhaps. She was shocked that her husband would commit infidelity and murder. It's enough of a reason to die."
Ayato: "But you have no proof?"
Inui: "...No one here talks about the curse. It's a theory I came up with when we couldn't get any decent testimony. It's unfortunate that we couldn't build a case on it."
*Inui stood up and picked up the kettle from the stove.*
Inui: "Tea?"
Ayato: "No, thank you."
*Inui refilled his cup with tea.*
Ayato: "...Have you learned anything about Satsuki's murder?"
Inui: "It doesn't look like the festival's had a Miko since then. I heard the Miko was supposed to dance for several years after her appearance, though."
Ayato: "Are you suggesting that Satsuki was the Miko?"
Inui: "What other possibilities are there?"
Ayato: "I believe I testified this at the time, but I watched the Miko's dance with Satsuki."
Inui: "But that was simply 'someone wearing the Miko's mask,' correct? It's hardly proof that Shigusa Satsuki wasn't the Miko."
*Ayato could say nothing in response.*
Inui: "I'm guessing she got caught up in some Shigusa trouble and was silenced for it. That's what it seems like from the way the Shigusas claimed they didn't know anything."
Ayato: "...And you have no proof of that either, do you?"
Inui: "...That's what I'm here to find."
*Was that even possible now?*
*It had been almost five years since Satsuki's murder, and before then... over 15 years had passed since Zaizen Keiko's.*
*There was no hope of definite proof remaining.*
*Nevertheless, Ayato had no intention of giving up.*

*They had, after all, been killed in a manner that matched the curse.*
*But what about Satsuki...?*
*When her body had been discovered, the people of the village all unanimously discussed it as if it was the curse as well.*
*But the body Ayato had seen was missing its limbs for some reason.*

*The night wore on without Ayato coming to any conclusions.*

====================05b_1225_05.txt====================
*One sheep,*
*two sheep,*
*three sheep, four...*
*A black shadow whispered on and on.*
*The words weren't an invitation to sleep.  The shadow was whispering to a girl lying on the ground with her eyes closed.*
*The girl's eyelids moved a little bit.  There was a creaking noise.*
*When the girl's eyes opened, she looked up at the black shadow.  It was a sheep.  Its head was covered in wool.  Its horns were twisted.  Its long, flattened pupils stared down at her.*
*The girl gasped and looked around.  She was surrounded by unfamiliar scenery.  She was on the shore of some island, and in the center of the island towered a steep mountain.*
"Where might I be?"
*The girl asked, staring at the sheep's eyes, artificial-looking like glass marbles.  If it were a normal sheep, it would never have understood her words.*
*However, the girl asked the sheep before her, for she knew that it had been the one whispering to her as she lay on the ground with her eyes closed.*
*Sure enough, the expressionless sheep moved its mouth as if feeding on grass and responded in a stern voice unimaginable from its appearance,*
"Welcome to the land of Purgatorio."
"Purgatorio?" asked the girl. "Is that the name of this island?"
*The sheep rose without an answer.  From the ground, the girl could only see its black legs.  They were unmistakably human legs.*
*The girl attempted to rise after the sheep. But she couldn't move as she wanted to. Looking down at her stiffened body, the girl screamed.*
*The girl's body had become that of a wooden doll.  Grains of wood adorned her bare feet, which shined as if her crafter had polished her many times.*
*Wooden balls had been inlaid in her elbows and knees to serve the function of her joints.  She couldn't move as she wanted to because they were grinding against her arms and thighs.*
*The creak she had heard when she opened her eyes was the sound of her own body moving.*
"What happened to my body?" asked the girl to the sheep man. "And who, exactly, am I?"
*"I'm sure you will come to learn those things." It wasn't the sheep man who had answered.  An angel had descended from above the girl at some point.*
*"What do you mean, Angel?" asked the girl to the angel fluttering about in the sky.*
*"First, you must overcome six trials," the angel answered solemnly.*
"But before that, you must wrap rushes around your waist and wash your face. It is necessary if you are to be accepted into Eden."
*"I understand, Angel." The girl spurred on her stiffened body and headed for the shore.  She washed her face and wrapped the rushes growing there around her waist.*
*Afterward, she felt her creaking body move easier.*
*"Now, let us go to the summit of Purgatorio."  The sheep man began to walk before the wooden girl.*

*This is why Toji has been investigating where the Congregation's money has been coming from.*
*If they're involved in the clinical trials, some third party such as a doctor or a hospital must be involved.*
*And if a third party is involved, there should be monetary exchange between them.*
*Even if most of its members are motivated by faith, the entire organization―especially its higher-ups―isn't.*
*They're motivated by a desire for prestige or money.*
*Looking at their account books makes that much clear.*
*The Blessed Congregation accepts donations from its members.*
*All sorts of numbers representing individual donations adorn the pages, from tens of yen to thousands.*
*She doesn't know the details, as the names of the donors aren't written down, but there are a few unusual points.*
*Twenty different people donated 5,000 yen on a single day.*
*This is clearly a division of a single 100,000 yen donation.*
*Of course, she has no proof...*
*Toji lights a cigarette.*
Toji: "Phew..."
*Sweet smoke rises from her mouth.*
*A donation of 100,000 yen.*
*A few times a year, the same amount is donated.*
*From what Toji has learned, most of the Blessed Congregation's faithful are poor.*
*Considering the story of how they took in Senri's faithful, it's difficult to believe that they have twenty members who are able to donate a whole month's wage like this.*
*It looks like these donations started around 1952.*
*Apparently, donations of roughly 60,000 to 80,000 are being broken up and recorded separately.*
*Are they using this money to support their needy members?*
*But there's also evidence to the contrary.*
*Leaving her cigarette in an ashtray, Toji flips to the expenses section of the account book and finds that much of their funds are being transferred to another organization.*
*No, perhaps "organization" is the wrong word.*
*It's a corporation in the same conglomeration as the Blessed Congregation.*
*This must be the "small jobs" Utsugi Keigo previously told her about.*
*The corporation runs a moneylending business.*
*So they lend out the money they collect from donations?*
*It's just Toji's shot in the dark, but they probably lend to faithful with low interest rates, and lend to anyone else with high rates.*
*This sort of individual moneylending is all too common now that banks can't give loans to individuals because of the post-war reconstruction.*
*There are plenty of fishy sorts doing this sort of lending too, since the laws haven't really progressed to keep up with it.*
*But it looks like this corporation the Blessed Congregation created is paying its taxes properly.*
*They would be under no obligation to pay taxes if they had remained a religious organization.*
*But since they've split into a for-profit entity and are paying taxes accordingly, it either means they're being managed decently or they're trying to look as if they are...*
*The Blessed Congregation also owns some charitable social service organizations.*
*Hospitals and orphanages, for instance.*
*These are things they didn't have as Senri.*
*There must be funds flowing to them as well.*
*Toji supposes that if they're involved with illicit clinical trials, this is probably where.*

*She sits up obediently.*

*What a frightening dream.*
*Only... it wasn't a dream.*
*It's still dark outside, before dawn.*
*She doesn't remember dreaming yesterday, so this is her first dream of the year.*
*The room is cold, mercilessly sapping Yukiko's body heat while she's covered in sweat.*
*She shivers again.*
*That was... not simply a dream.*

*She writes down the contents of her dream.*
*She has no memories of the events.*
*She has no memories... but they probably actually happened.*
*Yukiko's memories of her past are hazy.*
*Indeed, even her memories of her friend falling from that overpass are indistinct.*
*Was that dream a memory from that time?*
*If so... then what she's been denying all this time is meaningless.*
*She moves her pencil, writing everything down even while hoping it isn't true.*
*_I don't remember doing this... but if this helps me remember, then..._*

====================06b_0106_01.txt====================
*I'm dreaming.*
*I know it's a dream because I've seen this scenery countless times before.*
*I don't want to see it and yet... my left eye captures the scene perfectly.*
*In the darkness there's a boy and a girl.*
*They were both my friends.*
*There were many more boys and girls here... though I'm not sure if I'd call all of them friends.*
*But my eye sees only the two of them now.*
*The rest of the children are sleeping nearby, just like me.*
*Therefore, it's a dream.*
*I'm sleeping, yet I can see them, and there aren't any other people here.*
*The girl's hands touch the boy's throat.*
*I don't remember what the boy screamed, what the boy said.*
*But... things weren't normal.*
*Of course, strangling someone isn't something done within the bounds of reason.*
*I try to close my eye.*
*Even though I know it's a dream― No, because I know it's a dream, I don't want to see this any longer.*
*It's a repetition I'm unable to stop.*
*My eyelids don't move, as if they're fixed in place.*
*It's... the same as that time.*
*The girl's fingers dig into the boy's throat.*
*The boy's hands reach out to the girl.*
*The girl... is laughing.*
*The boy... is smiling.*
*Maybe they weren't smiles.*
*But from a distance, it looked to me as if the two of them were smiling.*
*The boy's arms drop to the floor.*
*The girl's hands leave his throat.*
*The girl embraces the husk of the boy.*
*And again... she laughs.*
*It's a scene I've seen countless times before.*
*Every time I see it, a filter like frosted glass appears before it, making it less distinct.*
*And yet... I never forget what happened then.*
*I can't forget, no matter what I do.*
*That's why I have these dreams...*

====================06c_0112_07.txt====================
*It's snowing.*
*Yukiko stands at the window, gazing at the sky.*
*The empty classroom is cold, her exhalations white.*
*Yukiko snuck out of the Blessed Congregation building to come here.*
*When Yukiko was given the opened letter and read it, this location immediately came to mind.*
*Yukiko herself doesn't really know how she came to that conclusion.*
*But she felt that she needed to come here as soon as possible.*
*She couldn't figure out the reason why, though.*
*She felt as though something was happening, and it scared her.*
*Something even scarier than being brought to the Blessed Congregation...*
Yukiko: "..."
*She gets dizzy and puts her hand on the window.*
*Occasionally she has these lapses in memory.*
*Ever since she started taking that medicine, she's been having those dreams that seem like lost memories.*
*Every one of them depicts frightening incidents.*
*Yukiko looks down at her hands.*
*These hands―they're drenched in sin.*
*From back then, long ago...*
*The door to the classroom opens and Yukiko reflexively recoils.*
*If a security guard's found her, she'll be thrown out.*
*She needs to avoid that.*
???: "...You came, Yukiko-chan."
*That voice.*
Yukiko: "Kohane-chan...?"
*Yukiko raises her head.*
Kohane: "...It's been a long time since you've called me by my name, Yukiko-chan."
Yukiko: "Ah... Yeah..."
*Yukiko doesn't know why she used Kohane's name.*
*She simply felt like she'd called her that a long time ago.*
*She can't even tell whether she doesn't remember... or whether she's starting to remember little by little.*
Kohane: "If you came here, then you understood the meaning of that poem, right?"
*Kohane approaches and stands behind Yukiko.*
Yukiko: "...Sunday evening, Ouba Academy..."
*She voices the words that come to her mind.*
Kohane: "...Right. It's easy enough to find if you take the beginnings and ends of the lines. ...Kind of a shame that I couldn't give a more accurate time and place, though."
*Kohane's reflection in the mirror smiles a little.*
Kohane: "But if you understood that... you must have remembered some stuff, right?"
Yukiko: "Huh...?"
Kohane: "You solved the code in the poem, and called me Kohane-chan..."
Yukiko: "U-Umm... Kohane-chan... I still don't..."
Kohane: "...We all ate candies together, didn't we?"
*Kohane keeps going, ignoring Yukiko's uncertainty.*
Kohane: "When they gave us those vaccines, they'd give us candy as a reward for being good... remember?"
Yukiko: "Did that... happen...?"
*She remembers getting shots.*
*It wasn't the pain, but the shock of the needle pricking her that made her almost cry... but someone consoled her.*
*Who was it...?*
Kohane: "...Have you remembered?"
*Kohane gazes into Yukiko's face.*
Yukiko: "...I don't know."
*All Yukiko can do is shake her head.*
Yukiko: "I don't know, but... I feel like that might have happened..."
*Was it Kohane who had consoled her then...?*
*...No, it wasn't.*
*The one who would stroke Yukiko's hair was...*
Kohane: "...Yukiko-chan."
*Kohane puts her hand on Yukiko's shoulder.*
Yukiko: "Wh― What...?"
Kohane: "...Please help me see Yukio-chan."
Yukiko: "Yukio...?"
*It's the first time Yukiko's heard that name in her present state.*
Kohane: "He's your brother, isn't he, Yukiko-chan? Why don't you... remember him?"
Yukiko: "I... don't know what to tell you..."
*She doesn't know what she doesn't know.*
*_But_, Yukiko thinks to herself.*
*_If I really had a brother, could I actually have forgotten about him?_*
Kohane: "Why... won't you let me see Yukio-chan...?"
*Kohane's grip gets stronger.*
Yukiko: "...I don't know― I don't know that person."
*Yukiko shakes her head over and over again.*
Kohane: "...How could you not know him? Are you that scared of me... taking Yukio-chan away from you...?"
*Kohane's hand on Yukiko's shoulder inches toward her neck.*
Yukiko: "No... Stop, Kohane-chan..."
*Yukiko tries to escape Kohane's hands, but she can't seem to move, as if she's in a dream.*
*...The scene before her seems to blend into the images she's seen in her dreams.*
*The one being strangled then was...*
*Yukiko hears the classroom door open as her consciousness begins to fade.*

*There's no surprise in her voice.*

*Shizuru's brother―Yuzuru.*
*I don't know his blood type, but if their parents were AA and AO, their children could be AA or AO as well.*
*If Yuzuru is type AO, he could have children with type O blood.*

*The blood drains from my head.*
*My vision blurs.*

Yukiko: "Ah―"

*Masaki rushes past me to Yukari.*
Yukiko: "Ah―"
*Yukiko falls to the floor, limp.*

*...We didn't make it.*
*We had foreseen that Yukiko would attack Yukari.*
*But why couldn't we have made it here earlier...?*
*Yukiko looks up at me where she lies on the floor.*
Yukiko: "Oh... Nii-san, what are you making that face for?"
*Her tone...*
*She looks up at me curiously.*
Reiji: "...Are you telling me you consumed Yukari?"
*The voice that comes out of my mouth is resigned.*
*She isn't Yukari.*
*She's the monster who killed her.*
*But... considering her circumstances, I can't even blame her for it.*
Yukiko: "Nii-san... let's go home."
*Yukiko takes my hand.*
*It's incredibly cold, and shivering slightly.*

*Where did the original persona of Kayahara Yukiko go?*

Reiji: "Just... stop..."

*Yet she keeps playing the part of Yukari.*
Reiji: "...You're not Yukari."
*Whispering those words is all I can do.*
*I can no longer free her from this obsession...*

====================07d_0121_00.txt====================
*January 21<sup>st</sup>, Tuesday.*
*After her discharge yesterday, Kyoko opened the shop up again immediately.*
*In the end, she accepted Fuyumi's proposal and repaid her debt.*
*Of course, since the company she'd borrowed the money from was affiliated with the Blessed Congregation, it made a simple round trip back to where it came from.*
*The Blessed Congregation itself became unable to carry on as an organization after its two primary leaders died.*
*After the police's compulsory investigation into their connection with the illegal clinical trials, the organization's downfall truly began.*
*With the remaining money, Fuyumi bought out the New Leaf Garden.*
*She had to, for the sake of the children that were being taken care of there.*
Kyoko: "What's Tokisaka-kun up to?"
*Kyoko asks Masaki as he sits next to the counter.*
Masaki: "He's busy with another matter. He didn't tell me what it was, saying it 'had nothing to do with me.'"
Kyoko: "I see... Need a refill?"
Masaki: "Sure."
*He sets his coffee cup down on the counter.*
Kyoko: "...If he's keeping quiet about it, it might not be work at all."
*Kyoko mutters, pouring fresh coffee into his cup.*
Masaki: "...He's got a lot of secrets, doesn't he? Work-related and otherwise."
Kyoko: "Well, he is a detective. There are a lot of things he can't tell people about."
Masaki: "That may be, but... you trust him, don't you?"
Kyoko: "We've known each other for a long time."
*Kyoko says, laughing.*
Kyoko: "He'll tell you what he needs to. If he doesn't, then it really doesn't have anything to do with you... or someone asked him not to."
Masaki: "...You think so?"
Kyoko: "Yeah. Right, Fuyumi-san?"
*She says to Fuyumi, who's sitting at the counter like Masaki.*
Fuyumi: "Huh? Y-Yeah."
*Fuyumi nods, flustered.*
*She's currently negotiating with the Shirosaki family to take in Michiru at the New Leaf Garden.*
*Michiru was too much for them to deal with.*
*Being followers of the Blessed Congregation, they took Michiru in when the White Lily Garden closed, but they left her in the hospital without looking after her for all this time.*
*Masaki doesn't understand why she's willing to do this much for Michiru.*
*No one's told him why, anyway.*
Fuyumi: "If he's not telling you, there's probably a reason for it."
*It sounds persuasive coming from her.*
*Masaki can't blame him, though.*
*He's hid many things and told many lies himself, after all.*
*_Is it a detective's job to expose people's secrets?_*
Kyoko: "Are you going to keep working for Tokisaka-kun, Masaki-kun?"
Masaki: "Well, yes... I intend to."
Kyoko: "Ayumu-chan'll be your rival, then."
Masaki: "'Rival'...? Isn't she still a student?"
Fuyumi: "Oh, think you can take it easy? I heard she played a big part in this case."
Masaki: "...Nah, I'm not really thinking about playing too big a part, myself."
*Masaki glances over at a table.*
*Yukari and Kohane―after her release from the hospital―sit there along with Ayumu.*
*Ayumu stands up after noticing Masaki's gaze.*
Ayumu: "Can I help you with something?"
Kyoko: "We were discussing who's a better detective's assistant: Ayumu-chan or Masaki-kun."
*Masaki doesn't recall having that conversation.*
Ayumu: "I think Masaki-san is far better than me."
Fuyumi: "...You're just being humble, right?"
Ayumu: "Of course."
*Ayumu agrees right away.*
Ayumu: "I've been his assistant longer."
Yukari: "...Only his 'self-proclaimed' assistant."
*Yukari comes over with an exasperated sigh.*
Kohane: "You'll still have to work harder, though, Masaki-san. Otherwise you'll get fired!"

Fuyumi: "I'll hire you if you get fired. Oh, but you'll have to live somewhere else."
Masaki: "...Well, thanks."
Fuyumi: "I need to leave a place for Yukiko to come back to, after all."
Masaki: "...That's right."
*She's living her life as Kayahara Fuyumi.*
*And he plans to live his life as Masaki Tomoyuki.*
*The story of the girl named Ayako and the boy named Hinagami Ayato came to a close long ago.*
Yukari: "Don't worry about it. You won't be dismissed, Masaki-san."
Kohane: "Huh? So you're on Team Masaki-san, Yukaricchi?"
*Kohane teases.*
Yukari: "That's not it... I think my brother trusts Masaki-san, that's all. Otherwise, he wouldn't let him live in his office."
